info.title: Duvo Public API
info.description:
Public API for programmatic access to Duvo. Authenticate with API keys created in the Duvo dashboard.

## Rate limits

Requests are counted per API key. Every response advertises the quota with the IETF RateLimit fields, so a client can self-throttle without waiting for a rejection:

- `RateLimit-Policy: "default";q=<quota>;w=<window seconds>` — the policy in force: `q` requests per `w` seconds.
- `RateLimit: "default";r=<remaining>;t=<seconds>` — the live state: `r` requests left, quota resetting in `t` seconds.
- Read the quota from the headers rather than hard-coding it; it differs per environment.
- The same numbers are also sent as `ratelimit-limit`, `ratelimit-remaining` and `ratelimit-reset`.

Once the quota is exhausted the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After` set to the seconds to wait; honor it instead of retrying immediately.

bearerAuth.description: API key authentication. Get your API key from the Duvo dashboard.

post.description: MCP JSON-RPC endpoint (Streamable HTTP transport). Exposes every public API route as an LLM-callable tool. The handshake (initialize, ping, tools/list) is open; tool calls require Bearer auth.

get.description: MCP Streamable HTTP: GET (server-initiated streaming) is not supported. Use POST. Without credentials it returns the RFC 9728 challenge so clients and scanners can discover the OAuth metadata.
List the memory files stored for an agent.

name.description: File name without its directory prefix

path.description: Relative path of the file within agent memory

generation.description: GCS object generation of the file's current contents

get.description: Get the contents of a single memory file for an agent.

parameters.description: Relative path to the memory file, e.g. notes.md or context/customer.md

path.description: Relative path of the file within agent memory

content.description: UTF-8 decoded contents of the file

generation.description: GCS object generation of the file's current contents

get.description: List plugins that can be referenced by name in a build's plugins array. Builds may also reference any public GitHub repository URL (https://github.com/owner/repo) as a plugin; those are not enumerated here.

name.description: Identifier to pass in the build's plugins array.

type.description: Plugin source. 'duvo-platform' plugins are pre-baked into the Duvo runtime; 'knowledge-work' plugins are role-oriented bundles (engineering, sales, legal, …) also baked into the runtime; 'github' plugins are downloaded from a user-supplied repository URL at run time.

post.description: Create a schedule for an agent. The schedule fires against the agent's live build. The authenticated user owns the schedule. On a team with versions, a repeating schedule for an Agent in an automation joins that automation's versions: one matching a schedule the automation already runs fires at once, and a new one is saved to the automation's draft and fires once the draft is made active (see `pending_change`).

get.description: List the schedules you own on an agent. Returns only your own schedules, whoever you are. Callers with an elevated team role can read every member's schedules on the agent, including who created each one, via `GET /agents/{agent_id}/schedules/all`.

schedules.description: Schedules the authenticated user owns on this agent. Never another member's, regardless of the caller's role — see `GET /agents/{agent_id}/schedules/all` for the elevated all-users read.

patch.description: Update fields on an existing schedule. Only supplied fields are changed; omitted fields retain their current values. Owners may update their own schedules; team superadmins may update any schedule on agents in the current team. A schedule that belongs to an automation with versions keeps firing as its automation's active version says: a change to its timing is saved to the automation's draft and takes effect when the draft is made active (see `pending_change`), while `enabled` applies at once.

delete.description: Delete a schedule. Owners may delete their own schedules; team superadmins may delete any schedule on agents in the current team. Deleting a schedule that belongs to an automation with versions stops it for its owner at once; the automation's versions keep the schedule for anyone else subscribed to it.

get.description: Get a team by ID. The caller must be scoped to the requested team.

id.description: Unique team identifier

name.description: Human-readable team name

organization_id.description: Parent organization ID, or null if the team is standalone

slack_team_id.description: Linked Slack workspace ID, or null if Slack is not connected

discovery_mode.description: How the team handles agent discovery

automations_migrated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the team's move to the Automations workspace, or null if it has not moved

automation_revisions_migrated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the team's move to automation revisions, or null. Narrower than automations_migrated_at: a team can be on the workspace without revisions

post.description: Start an OAuth-based connection with a native provider (Gmail, Google Sheets, Outlook, etc.). The provider path parameter is the native OAuth provider key from listIntegrations, not the integration type. Returns an authorization URL that must be opened in a browser by a human end-user; once they grant consent, Duvo creates the matching connection and redirects the browser to the optional `return_url` (or the Duvo dashboard if none is provided). Poll `/v2/teams/:team_id/connections` to detect the new connection.

return_url.description: Where to send the user's browser after OAuth completes.

reconnect_instance_id.description: When set, the OAuth flow will update the existing connection in place rather than creating a new one.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: Native OAuth provider key, not the integration type. Use oauth_provider_key from listIntegrations (for example, google_gmail for integration type gmail, google_sheets for googlesheets, or microsoft_outlook for outlook); passing an integration type returns 404 "Unknown OAuth provider".

authorization_url.description: OAuth provider authorization URL to open in a browser

post.description: Start an OAuth-based connection with a remote MCP server using Dynamic Client Registration. Returns an authorization URL the user must open in a browser; once they grant consent, Duvo creates the matching connection and redirects the browser to the optional `returnUrl`.

mcp_server_url.description: URL of the MCP server requiring OAuth.

name.description: Human-readable name to display for the connection.

custom_integration_id.description: Optional ID of a custom integration this connection should be associated with.

return_url.description: Where to send the user's browser after consent completes. Accepts an absolute URL on a domain Duvo allows, or a path relative to the Duvo frontend (e.g. `/integrations/slack`).

integration_type.description: Optional catalog integration type (e.g. `netsuite`, `asana`). When it names a known MCP OAuth catalog integration and `mcp_server_url` matches that integration's registered server, the connection is treated as a catalog connection; otherwise it requires the custom MCP servers capability.

reconnect_instance_id.description: When set, the OAuth flow will update the existing connection in place rather than creating a new one.

oauth_client_id.description: OAuth client ID of a client the user registered on the authorization server themselves (e.g. a NetSuite Integration record). Takes precedence over preregistered credentials and Dynamic Client Registration. Cannot be combined with custom_integration_id. On reconnect, omit to reuse the connection's stored credentials, or provide to replace (rotate) them.

oauth_client_secret.description: Client secret for `oauth_client_id`. Omit for public clients (PKCE-only).

authorization_url.description: OAuth provider authorization URL to open in a browser

post.description: Probe an MCP server URL to discover whether it supports OAuth Dynamic Client Registration. Returns the authorization endpoint and required scopes when supported. Useful as a precursor to `/v2/teams/:team_id/connections/oauth/mcp/start` or `/v2/teams/:team_id/connections`. Performs no writes.

mcp_server_url.description: URL of the MCP server to probe for OAuth support.

supports_dcr.description: True if the MCP server advertises OAuth Dynamic Client Registration

authorization_endpoint.description: OAuth authorization endpoint advertised by the MCP server, when discoverable

scopes.description: Scopes the MCP server requests during authorization

get.description: List your Duvo Pulse dashboards (live, agent-generated visualizations of your Duvo data). Ordered most recently updated first, except scope=automation, which is ordered by creation time (then id) so the whole scope can be read with the after_id cursor without a concurrent change shifting a page boundary.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of results per page (1-100, default 20)

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Which dashboards to return: 'created' (yours, the default), 'team' (published to your whole team by a teammate), 'shared' (shared with you individually by a teammate), or 'automation' (owned by one of your team's automations, each carrying its automation's name).

parameters.name: after_id
parameters.description: Keyset cursor for reading the whole 'automation' scope: the id of the last dashboard you received; returns the page after it in (created_at, id) order. Use this instead of 'offset' when reading every page, so a dashboard created, updated or deleted between requests cannot shift a page boundary you have already passed. 400 when the id no longer names a dashboard (restart from the first page). Only valid with scope=automation.

automation_name.description: Name of the owning automation, resolved only on the `automation` list scope — the one surface that renders the composite `<Automation> / <Title>` label. Absent elsewhere; a client reads absence and null the same way.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

post.description: Create a new Duvo Pulse dashboard from a natural-language prompt (e.g. 'open cases by queue this week') and dispatch the first generation turn. Generation is asynchronous — poll GET /artifacts/{artifactId} until status is completed. The dashboard is private to you unless you set visibility to 'team', which shares it with your whole team straight away — with permission 'view' (teammates see the dashboard) or 'edit' (teammates can also iterate on it).

get.description: Get a Duvo Pulse dashboard's metadata and generation status. When status is completed and html_code_present is true, fetch the rendered HTML from GET /artifacts/{artifactId}/render; the conversation is served by GET /artifacts/{artifactId}/messages.

automation_name.description: Name of the owning automation, resolved only on the `automation` list scope — the one surface that renders the composite `<Automation> / <Title>` label. Absent elsewhere; a client reads absence and null the same way.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

pending_question.description: The question an update of this dashboard is paused on, waiting for the user's answer, or null when no update is waiting or the caller cannot edit the dashboard. The status stays running while it waits.

tool_call_id.description: The question's toolCallId, which POST /artifacts/{artifactId}/answer takes.

questions.description: The text of each question the update is waiting on.

patch.description: Update a Duvo Pulse dashboard's settings — rename it. Only the creator can update it.

automation_name.description: Name of the owning automation, resolved only on the `automation` list scope — the one surface that renders the composite `<Automation> / <Title>` label. Absent elsewhere; a client reads absence and null the same way.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

delete.description: Delete a Duvo Pulse dashboard. Only the creator can delete it.

get.description: Discover queues the current editor may connect to this team-created Pulse before sampling data. Requires live dashboard edit permission and ordinary team data access. Module sources are installed with the Module. A queue ID in generated code does not grant access.

parameters.name: artifact_id
parameters.description: Current Pulse artifact ID, supplied by the builder or viewer context.

put.description: Connect an authorized same-team queue to a team-created Pulse before sampling it. Idempotent. This bounds dashboard data access; it never grants Process membership or case-action authority. Requires both edit permission and ordinary team source access.

parameters.name: artifact_id
parameters.description: Current Pulse artifact ID, supplied by the builder or viewer context.

delete.description: Disconnect a source from a team-created dashboard. Subsequent dashboard reads and writes immediately lose access. Idempotent; does not delete the queue or cases.

parameters.name: artifact_id
parameters.description: Current Pulse artifact ID, supplied by the builder or viewer context.

get.description: Serve a Duvo Pulse dashboard's rendered HTML document (text/html, not JSON). 404 until the first generation turn has produced HTML.

Render a Duvo Pulse dashboard to a PDF document (application/pdf, not JSON). 404 until the first generation turn has produced HTML; 409 for an openui dashboard, whose substrate this exporter cannot render.

Render a Duvo Pulse dashboard to a self-contained static HTML snapshot (text/html, data baked in). 404 until the first generation turn has produced HTML; 409 for an openui dashboard, whose substrate this exporter cannot render.

post.description: Publish (share) a Duvo Pulse dashboard to your whole team or your whole organization, or revert it to private (creator only). When publishing, set permission to 'view' (teammates see the dashboard) or 'edit' (teammates can also iterate on it); organization-wide viewers outside the team always get view-only access.

automation_name.description: Name of the owning automation, resolved only on the `automation` list scope — the one surface that renders the composite `<Automation> / <Title>` label. Absent elsewhere; a client reads absence and null the same way.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

post.description: Duplicate a Duvo Pulse dashboard, producing an idle clone of the current rendered dashboard. The conversation history, shares, and connections are not copied.

automation_name.description: Name of the owning automation, resolved only on the `automation` list scope — the one surface that renders the composite `<Automation> / <Title>` label. Absent elsewhere; a client reads absence and null the same way.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

post.description: Send an instruction to iterate on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (e.g. 'make it a bar chart', 'filter to last 14 days'). The creator can always iterate; teammates can too when the Pulse is published to the team with edit access. The agent regenerates asynchronously — poll GET /artifacts/{artifactId} for status.

attachments.description: Attachments to hand the agent, uploaded beforehand via the upload-urls endpoint (max 5)

missingAttachmentIds.description: Attachment ids that are no longer usable and must be re-uploaded. Present only when the conflict was caused by attachments.

get.description: List the chat transcript of a Duvo Pulse dashboard's live version (requires edit access). Returns the most recent page by default, oldest first within the page; pass `before` (a message id from a previous page) to walk back through older messages. Messages from other version branches are not included.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of messages to return (1-500, default 50).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Message id cursor: return the page of messages immediately older than this message. Omit for the most recent page.

post.description: Issue a presigned upload URL for a file to attach to a Duvo Pulse dashboard message (e.g. an HTML dashboard to copy, or a screenshot to match). POST the file bytes to the returned upload_url as multipart form data under the field name 'file', then pass the returned attachment_id in the attachments array of POST /artifacts/{artifactId}/messages. The agent reads the file directly from its sandbox. Files live as long as the dashboard's sandbox (about 12 hours), so upload shortly before sending.

filename.description: Name of the file being attached, without any path segments

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file, e.g. text/html or image/png

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes (max 25MB)

attachment_id.description: Echo this back in the message body's attachments array

sandbox_id.description: Sandbox the file will be uploaded into

sandbox_path.description: Absolute path the file will occupy inside the sandbox

upload_url.description: Presigned URL to POST the file bytes to as multipart form data

expires_in_seconds.description: Seconds until upload_url stops being accepted

post.summary: Create Pulse Dashboard Attachment Upload URL

get.description: Mint a short-lived presigned URL to download or preview a file attached to a Duvo Pulse dashboard message. Returns 404 once the dashboard's sandbox has expired and the file is gone (about 12 hours).

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The attachment to mint a download URL for

download_url.description: Presigned URL to GET the file bytes from

expires_in_seconds.description: Seconds until download_url stops being accepted

get.summary: Get Pulse Dashboard Attachment Download URL

post.description: Trigger an on-demand data refresh of a Duvo Pulse dashboard. The dashboard regenerates its connection-sourced values in the background — poll GET /artifacts/{artifactId} for status.

automation_name.description: Name of the owning automation, resolved only on the `automation` list scope — the one surface that renders the composite `<Automation> / <Title>` label. Absent elsewhere; a client reads absence and null the same way.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

post.description: Stop an in-flight Duvo Pulse generation turn. Requires edit access to the dashboard. Flips the dashboard to 'interrupted' and keeps any streamed-so-far reply; stopping when nothing is generating is a successful no-op.

partial_text.description: The assistant text streamed so far, kept in the conversation as the partial reply. Omit when calling from an API client without streaming state.

automation_name.description: Name of the owning automation, resolved only on the `automation` list scope — the one surface that renders the composite `<Automation> / <Title>` label. Absent elsewhere; a client reads absence and null the same way.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

get.description: List the connections (data sources) attached to a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires edit access).

post.description: Attach one of your connections (data sources) to a Duvo Pulse dashboard so the agent can use its tools (requires edit access).

delete.description: Detach a connection (data source) from a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires edit access).

post.description: Answer a pending question the Duvo Pulse agent asked and resume the paused run (creator or team editors). Use the toolCallId from the dashboard's message transcript.

get.description: List the comment threads on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires view access). Each thread carries its author, the dashboard element it is pinned to, its replies oldest-first, and whether it has been marked complete.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of comment threads to return (1-200, default 50).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of comment threads to skip, for paging.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only threads in this state: `open` for threads not yet marked complete, `complete` for those that are. Omit for both. `total` and `open_total` always count the whole set, so a filtered page still reports how many threads exist.

post.description: Start a comment thread on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires view access). Pass `element` — captured from the dashboard canvas — to pin the thread to one element; omit it for a comment on the dashboard as a whole.

Reply to a comment thread on a Duvo Pulse dashboard (requires view access). `commentId` must be a thread root; threads are one level deep. A thread already marked complete still accepts replies and stays complete.

Mark a Duvo Pulse dashboard comment thread complete, or reopen it (requires view access). Pass the target state in `resolved`; the call is idempotent, and the response carries the thread with `resolved_at` and `resolved_by` set or cleared.

delete.description: Delete a comment or reply on a Duvo Pulse dashboard. Allowed for the comment's author and for the dashboard's creator. Deleting a thread root keeps its replies, rendered under a deleted opening comment.

get.description: List the version history of a Duvo Pulse dashboard, newest first (requires edit access). Use the version id with the restore and version-render endpoints.

content_format.description: The substrate the dashboard is written in. New substrates are added over time.

get.description: Serve a specific version's rendered HTML document for a Duvo Pulse dashboard (text/html, requires edit access).

post.description: Restore a previous version of a Duvo Pulse dashboard, making it live again (requires edit access). Non-destructive — it moves the head pointer to the chosen version.
Create a new sandbox for file uploads. The returned sandbox_id can be passed to POST /v2/teams/:team_id/runs to stage data for a run.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the sandbox will expire

post.description: Get a presigned URL for uploading a file into a sandbox. Use for files larger than 10MB; smaller files can be uploaded directly via POST /v2/sandboxes/:sandbox_id/files.

path.description: Path where the file will be uploaded (e.g. /workspace/data.csv)
Path the file will be uploaded to

expires_in_seconds.description: Seconds until the presigned URL expires

get.description: List files in a sandbox directory.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Directory to list files from (defaults to /workspace)

name.description: File or directory name (basename)

path.description: Absolute path inside the sandbox

type.description: Whether this entry is a regular file or a directory

size_bytes.description: Size of the file in bytes (0 for directories)

files.description: Entries in the requested directory

post.description: Upload a file directly to the sandbox. Maximum file size is 10MB. For larger files, use POST /v2/sandboxes/:sandbox_id/upload-urls.

path.description: Path the file was uploaded to

size_bytes.description: Size of the uploaded file in bytes

get.description: Get the latest evaluation analysis for a specific agent run (Run).

rubrics.description: The Agent-specific rubrics this evaluation scored, as they were when the Run was judged.

get.description: Aggregate evaluation counts and flag distribution for an Assignment's Jobs since the given timestamp.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only Jobs evaluated after this are counted

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: When 'custom', only counts Jobs scored against the target revision's custom rubrics, and only `custom__*` rubric flags. Defaults to 'all' (platform + custom rubrics).

parameters.name: revision_id
parameters.description: Target a specific Assignment revision instead of the live revision. Only honoured when scope='custom' — non-custom scopes aggregate across all revisions. Defaults to the live revision when omitted.

get.description: List the evaluation rubrics a Run is scored against: the platform default rubrics plus the Agent-specific rubrics for a build. Defaults to the Agent's live build; pass build_id to target the revision a specific Run ran against.

parameters.name: build_id
parameters.description: Return rubrics for this specific build (the revision a Run ran against). Defaults to the agent's live build when omitted.

post.description: Add one Agent-specific evaluation rubric to a build. A build may hold at most 5 custom rubrics by default (25 on teams with the newer rubric generator enabled); this fails with 409 once the build's ceiling is reached, and the error message states it. Defaults to the Agent's live build; pass build_id to target a specific revision.

title.description: Short, human-readable Pass/Fail rubric title.

description.description: A 1-2 sentence Pass condition phrased as a question.

build_id.description: Add the rubric to this build (revision). Defaults to the agent's live build when omitted.

selected_automation_revision_id.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

put.description: Replace a build's entire Agent-specific evaluation rubric set in one call (at most 5 rubrics by default, 25 on teams with the newer rubric generator enabled). Existing custom rubrics are removed and the supplied list becomes the new set; pass an empty array to clear them. Defaults to the Agent's live build; pass build_id to target a specific revision.

title.description: Short, human-readable Pass/Fail rubric title.

description.description: A 1-2 sentence Pass condition phrased as a question.

rubrics.description: The complete custom rubric set for the build. Replaces every existing custom rubric; pass an empty array to clear them.

build_id.description: Replace the custom rubrics on this build (revision). Defaults to the agent's live build when omitted.

selected_automation_revision_id.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

patch.description: Edit a single Agent-specific evaluation rubric's title and/or description. The edit produces a NEW rubric (with a new id and slug) so previously scored Runs stay attributed to the original criterion; the response contains the new rubric.

title.description: Short, human-readable Pass/Fail rubric title.

description.description: A 1-2 sentence Pass condition phrased as a question.

selected_automation_revision_id.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

delete.description: Remove a single Agent-specific evaluation rubric. Future Runs on the build are no longer scored against it.

parameters.name: selected_automation_revision_id
parameters.description: The automation revision this edit is being made at. Pass a draft and the edit is folded into that draft itself; pass the active revision and the edit lands on a draft branched from it. A historic revision is rejected — it cannot be activated from without an explicit rebase. A revision belonging to a different automation is ignored, and the edit targets the automation the addressed agent belongs to. Omit to target the automation's active revision.

get.description: List every team member's schedules on an agent, including who created each one. Requires an elevated team role; callers without one receive 403 and should use `GET /agents/{agent_id}/schedules`, which returns only the schedules they own.

schedules.description: Every schedule on this agent, across all team members. Each row carries `user_id` plus the `user_name` and `user_email` of the member who created it.

truncated.description: True when the agent has more schedules than one response can carry and some were omitted. The rows returned are the oldest by `created_at`.

get.description: List the case triggers configured for an agent. Each trigger automatically dispatches the agent to run cases added to a queue.

pending_change.description: On a team with versions, a change to this trigger saved to the automation's draft. The trigger keeps its current values until the draft is made active. Null when nothing is waiting.

automation_revision_id.description: The automation's draft revision that holds the change

case_queue_id.description: The queue the draft routes to this agent, or null when the draft takes the trigger away

enabled.description: Whether the trigger will be on once the draft is made active

post.description: Create a case trigger for an agent. An agent may have at most one case trigger; this returns 409 if one already exists.

case_queue_id.description: Queue whose new cases should trigger this agent

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is active. Disabled triggers do not dispatch runs.

concurrency.description: Concurrency cap for the target queue. The cap is queue-wide, so this affects every Agent working the queue, not just this trigger. Only 1 (run cases one at a time) or null (reset the whole queue's cap to the platform default) can be set here; higher caps are configured per-queue via PATCH /v2/admin/case-queues/{queueId}/concurrency. Omit to leave the queue's current cap unchanged.

pending_change.description: On a team with versions, a change to this trigger saved to the automation's draft. The trigger keeps its current values until the draft is made active. Null when nothing is waiting.

automation_revision_id.description: The automation's draft revision that holds the change

case_queue_id.description: The queue the draft routes to this agent, or null when the draft takes the trigger away

enabled.description: Whether the trigger will be on once the draft is made active

get.description: Preview which other agents would conflict with this agent's case trigger if it pointed at the given queue. Does not modify the trigger.

parameters.name: case_queue_id
parameters.description: The queue to check for conflicts against

get.description: Retrieve a single case trigger by id.

automation_revision_id.description: The automation's draft revision that holds the change

case_queue_id.description: The queue the draft routes to this agent, or null when the draft takes the trigger away

enabled.description: Whether the trigger will be on once the draft is made active

case_queue_id.description: Queue whose new cases should trigger this agent

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is active. Disabled triggers do not dispatch runs.

concurrency.description: Concurrency cap for the trigger's queue. The cap is queue-wide, so this affects every Agent working the queue, not just this trigger. Only 1 (run cases one at a time) or null (reset the whole queue's cap to the platform default) can be set here; higher caps are configured per-queue via PATCH /v2/admin/case-queues/{queueId}/concurrency. Omit to leave the current value unchanged.

automation_revision_id.description: The automation's draft revision that holds the change

case_queue_id.description: The queue the draft routes to this agent, or null when the draft takes the trigger away

enabled.description: Whether the trigger will be on once the draft is made active

delete.description: Delete a case trigger. Only the trigger creator or a builder/admin can delete it.

get.description: List the trigger definitions the authenticated user owns on an agent (Agent in the Duvo UI). Triggers start a Run automatically when an external event fires (e.g. an email arrives or a Linear issue is created).

pending_change.description: Set on a trigger that belongs to an automation with versions when its draft changes this trigger. Null otherwise.

automation_revision_id.description: The automation's draft revision that holds the change.

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is on once the draft is made active. Null when the draft removes it.

filter_config.description: The filter the trigger uses once the draft is made active. Null when the draft removes it.

put.description: Create or update the authenticated user's trigger for an integration on an agent. The integration must already be connected to the agent (its OAuth connection set up in the Duvo dashboard). Set `enabled: false` to pause a trigger without deleting it. An agent holds one trigger per integration for a user, so a save with a different `trigger_type` replaces the existing one — except when that trigger is an @mention trigger, which is managed from the agent's mention setting and answers 409 (`mention_trigger_protected`) here. @mention triggers are best managed from that setting throughout: this route leaves an existing one's `filter_config` untouched, and refuses to create a `teams_mention` trigger without a `filter_config.tenantId` (400, `mention_trigger_workspace_required`) — a Slack mention trigger has no equivalent field to supply.

integration_slug.description: Integration slug the trigger fires for (e.g. `gmail`, `outlook`, `linear-native`, `google-drive`).

trigger_type.description: Trigger type within the integration (e.g. `email_received`). Discover valid values via the trigger types endpoint. Integrations that enumerate their trigger types (Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, Google Sheets) reject anything else with 400 (`trigger_type_unsupported`), except a save that pauses a trigger already carrying that type.

filter_config.description: Integration-specific filter config (e.g. sender/subject filters). Shape comes from the integration's filter schema. Replaces the trigger's current config, so send the whole object — except on an @mention trigger, whose config is managed from the agent's mention setting and is left as it is.

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is active. Defaults to true.

pending_change.description: Set on a trigger that belongs to an automation with versions when its draft changes this trigger. Null otherwise.

automation_revision_id.description: The automation's draft revision that holds the change.

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is on once the draft is made active. Null when the draft removes it.

filter_config.description: The filter the trigger uses once the draft is made active. Null when the draft removes it.

webhook_status.description: Whether the upstream webhook this trigger needs is registered. Null when the save needed no webhook work: every trigger type but Jira today, and a Jira save with `enabled: false`. Every enabled Jira save reconciles, so saving again retries a failed registration. `registered` means Duvo holds a current subscription covering this trigger's projects. `connection_required` means the Jira Connection this trigger is bound to names no Atlassian site, so there is nothing to register against; reconnect Jira and save again. `project_not_found` means Jira found no project for one of `filter_config.project_keys` that the Connection can open, so that key is left out of the webhook; check the keys and save again. `failed` means Atlassian refused or the call did not complete; see `webhook_error` and retry. The trigger row is saved in every case; anything but `registered` means it will not fire yet.

webhook_error.description: On `failed`, a stable reason code for the refusal (for example `http_403`, `rejected_by_jira`). `conflict_other_binding` means the Connection's Jira account already sends events to another Duvo Connection, in this team or another, and Jira allows one per account; connect a different Jira account. `issue_created_unconfirmed` means Jira has not yet confirmed that the webhook sends new issues, so they may not start Runs; Duvo tries again about every two hours, and saving again tries at once. Null otherwise.

code.description: Stable discriminator for errors a client must tell apart. `connection_missing_scopes` means the bound connection's OAuth grant lacks a scope this trigger needs and must be reconnected. `trigger_type_unsupported` means the integration enumerates its trigger types and `trigger_type` is not one of them, so the trigger could never fire; the message lists the types it does have, and the trigger types endpoint is the general source. A trigger that already carries such a type can still be paused (`enabled: false`, same `trigger_type`) and deleted. `jira_watched_fields_required` means a Jira save that enables or creates the trigger carried no readable watched field in `filter_config.fields` and was not a new-issues trigger (`filter_config.issue_created: true` with no `fields`), so the trigger could never start a Run; send at least one readable field id, or turn on new issues and send no fields. An existing Jira trigger can still be paused without either. `jira_project_keys_required` means such a save carried no project key in `filter_config.project_keys`; send at least one. `jira_project_keys_limit` means it carried more than 50, which is one Jira lookup page. `mention_trigger_protected` means the trigger this save would replace is an @mention trigger, which only the agent's mention setting may change; delete it to free the integration. `mention_trigger_workspace_required` means this save would create a `teams_mention` trigger with no `filter_config.tenantId`, which would match no inbound mention; turn @mentions on from the agent's mention setting, which resolves the tenant from the team's Teams workspace, or send `tenantId` explicitly. Only Teams mention triggers pin a workspace this way — a Slack one needs no such field. `trigger_save_timed_out` means the save did not finish inside the bound this route holds while writing the trigger; nothing is wrong with the request, so retry it.

integration_instance_id.description: On `connection_missing_scopes`, the connection that was rejected — the one to reconnect. Several connections can be bound to one agent, so this names which.

409.description: `mention_trigger_protected`: the trigger this save would replace is an @mention trigger and the requested `trigger_type` differs. Delete that trigger (`DELETE /v1/triggers/{agentId}/{triggerId}`, id from `GET /v1/triggers/{agentId}`) to use the integration for a different trigger type. `trigger_save_timed_out`: the save did not finish inside the bound this route holds while writing the trigger — retry. Without either code, the integration already has a trigger on this agent and the save simply collided.

post.description: Create a Slack channel trigger on an agent (Agent in the Duvo UI): the agent starts a Run whenever a matching message is posted in the channel. An agent can carry one trigger per channel, so call this once per channel. The Slack workspace must be installed for the team AND bound to the agent's live build first (see the Slack bound-workspaces endpoint) — otherwise this returns 400.

trigger_type.description: Trigger type. Only `slack_channel_message` (a message posted in a Slack channel) is supported here.

slack_team_id.description: Slack workspace (team) ID the channel belongs to, e.g. `T0123ABCD`. Defaults to the team's default installed workspace. Discover the workspaces an agent can use with the bound-workspaces endpoint.

channel_id.description: Slack channel ID to watch, e.g. `C0123ABCD`.

channel_name.description: Slack channel name shown in Duvo, without the leading `#`, e.g. `support-inbox`.

oneOf.description: Fire on every message posted in the channel.

values.description: Case-insensitive keywords; a message fires the trigger when it contains any of them. Duplicates are deduplicated.

oneOf.description: Fire only on messages containing one of the keywords.

match_rule.description: Which channel messages fire the trigger: `{"kind":"all"}` for every message, or `{"kind":"contains","values":["invoice"]}` to match keywords.

is_private.description: Whether the channel is private. Defaults to false. Private channels require the Duvo Slack app to be invited to the channel.

integration_instance_id.description: Specific bound Slack connection to run the trigger off. Omit to use your own connection, or pass one returned by the bound-workspaces endpoint.

filter_config.description: The filter the trigger uses once the draft is made active. Null when the draft removes it.

patch.description: Update a Slack channel trigger you own — repoint it at another channel, change which messages match, or pause and resume it with `enabled`. Only the supplied fields change. Resuming a paused trigger requires the Slack connection it runs off to still be available on the agent; changing the channel resets the trigger's seen-message state.

channel_id.description: New Slack channel ID to watch. Omit to leave unchanged.

channel_name.description: New Slack channel name, without the leading `#`.

oneOf.description: Fire on every message posted in the channel.

values.description: Case-insensitive keywords; a message fires the trigger when it contains any of them. Duplicates are deduplicated.

oneOf.description: Fire only on messages containing one of the keywords.

match_rule.description: Which channel messages fire the trigger: `{"kind":"all"}` for every message, or `{"kind":"contains","values":["invoice"]}` to match keywords.

enabled.description: Set to false to pause the trigger without deleting it, or true to resume it. Resuming requires the connection the trigger uses to still be available on the agent.

get.description: Get a single automation with its agent and queue counts, the tab arrangement its detail view navigates by, and `links` to each tab it has right now.

code_step_count.description: How many of the agent_count members are code steps rather than agents. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason is_setting_up is.

folder_id.description: The agent folder this automation sits in, or null when it sits at the root. Automations reuse the team's existing agent_folder tree rather than a parallel one, so a converted team keeps the grouping it already had. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason is_setting_up is: the client parses this response, and a backend that predates the column must not throw and take the automation's name down with it.

pinned_at.description: When the calling user pinned this automation to the top of their Automations list, or null when they have not. A pin is per user, like an Agent pin: teammates each keep their own. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason folder_id is.

is_setting_up.description: True while this Module automation's setup is under way. setup_started_at is stamped when the team starts setting up (and again by reopen-setup) and cleared when setup finishes, so this reads as currently in setup, not as a record of a past one. Read together with is_demo, which lives on the detail response: both true is a demo with a build under way; is_demo alone is a demo nobody has begun. On the summary rather than the detail so that a client holding only a list, create or patch response knows the state too, and so every write onto the shared automation collection carries it. Defaulted rather than required: the client parses this response, so a backend that predates the column must not throw and take the automation's name down with it, and nothing on the wire has always meant an automation nobody has set up.

setup_step.description: The key of the latest confirmed setup step, null until Start Setup is pressed. The server only ever advances it forward, so reopening a setup can resume where the team got to. Cleared with the rest of the setup state when setup finishes.

setup_build_chat_id.description: The Ask Duvo chat building the automation from the approved proposal, or null while setup has not reached the build. Not a hard reference: the chat can be deleted while this still names it, which the client reads as no build yet.

setup_progress.description: The setup facts behind the tile's Setup badge — captures uploaded, the team's own process map generated, a proposal written — or null while the automation is not being set up (and whenever it has no module process for the facts to hang off).

viewer_can_edit.description: Whether the caller may change this automation. An automation takes its agents' ownership rule: a Builder may edit one whose every agent they created, and Lead Builder or above may edit any. Sent by the list and detail endpoints; absent from create and update responses, where the client falls back to the caller's role.

live_revision_number.description: Number of the live revision, or null when none is live. It is a number, not a history the user can open: revision history is shown only on the Revisions tab, so when asked for it and `links` has no `revisions`, first say this Automation has no Revisions tab.

module_template_slug.description: Slug of the Module template this Automation was created from, or null. Permanent provenance — it survives setup and is not cleared.

module_template_version.description: Version of that template, set alongside the slug.

clarity_process_id.description: The Clarity process this Automation runs: its Module's process, or the one it was built from. Null when it runs none. Its map is what the Process tab shows. Defaulted for a backend that predates the field.

process_node_id.description: The process identity this Automation pins, which its People roles hang off. Null when it has none: its team has no organization, or a Module automation is not linked to its process yet.

is_demo.description: True while this is an unconverted Module demo: its data is sample data and it cannot run. Cleared when the demo is converted into a real automation, which is irreversible and either deletes the sample cases and Runs or closes them out as history. Starting setup does not clear it: that only records that setup began.

has_draft.description: Whether an open draft revision exists. Always false for an automation without revisions: an automation-level draft badge is a revision concept, and the agent builder surfaces its own draft build state.

post.description: Duplicate an automation into a new one named "Copy of <name>", copying what it runs today: its live agents and builds, its queues (empty), the routing and handovers between them, and each agent's Memory when the team holds Memory and the agent has it on. The caller's own triggers and schedules are copied switched off, so the copy starts no run until they turn them on; other members' triggers and schedules are not copied. An automation built by hand also gets its Policy: sections, questions, answers, and which agents read them. Cases and run history are not copied. A Module demo, and a Module automation with Policy questions, can't be duplicated.

code_step_count.description: How many of the agent_count members are code steps rather than agents. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason is_setting_up is.

folder_id.description: The agent folder this automation sits in, or null when it sits at the root. Automations reuse the team's existing agent_folder tree rather than a parallel one, so a converted team keeps the grouping it already had. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason is_setting_up is: the client parses this response, and a backend that predates the column must not throw and take the automation's name down with it.

pinned_at.description: When the calling user pinned this automation to the top of their Automations list, or null when they have not. A pin is per user, like an Agent pin: teammates each keep their own. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason folder_id is.

is_setting_up.description: True while this Module automation's setup is under way. setup_started_at is stamped when the team starts setting up (and again by reopen-setup) and cleared when setup finishes, so this reads as currently in setup, not as a record of a past one. Read together with is_demo, which lives on the detail response: both true is a demo with a build under way; is_demo alone is a demo nobody has begun. On the summary rather than the detail so that a client holding only a list, create or patch response knows the state too, and so every write onto the shared automation collection carries it. Defaulted rather than required: the client parses this response, so a backend that predates the column must not throw and take the automation's name down with it, and nothing on the wire has always meant an automation nobody has set up.

setup_step.description: The key of the latest confirmed setup step, null until Start Setup is pressed. The server only ever advances it forward, so reopening a setup can resume where the team got to. Cleared with the rest of the setup state when setup finishes.

setup_build_chat_id.description: The Ask Duvo chat building the automation from the approved proposal, or null while setup has not reached the build. Not a hard reference: the chat can be deleted while this still names it, which the client reads as no build yet.

setup_progress.description: The setup facts behind the tile's Setup badge — captures uploaded, the team's own process map generated, a proposal written — or null while the automation is not being set up (and whenever it has no module process for the facts to hang off).

An automation takes its agents' ownership rule: a Builder may edit one whose every agent they created, and Lead Builder or above may edit any. get.description: What still has to be set up before an automation can run on real work. Call this first for a readiness question ("what do I still need to set up", "is it ready to run", "why isn't it running") and before checking an automation's Connections, Logins or Secrets one by one. Each of `items` is `{ key, label, status: ok | missing | broken, detail, link, link_tab }` and covers one of: required Policy questions still open, Connections with no working account pinned or that need reconnecting, Logins and Secrets (present or missing, never their values), Queue slots with no Queue linked, Queues with routing off, no Agent or an Agent with no live version, what starts it (a Trigger, a Schedule, or Cases added to a routed Queue), the live revision and a pending draft, and whether it is still a demo. Lead with what is `missing` or `broken`, each with its own `link` (named by `link_tab`); never build a link. Quote counts from `summary`, including `connections_to_fix`, rather than counting items. `ready` is null when the caller can't read the Policy; `note` then says what to tell the user. A Connection only the caller can see counts for the caller. When `links_note` is present, give no link to the automation at all. Each `link` is a path in the Duvo web app; give the user the full URL beside it (`url`, and `urls` for `links`).

get.description: The figures a Module automation's Pulse dashboards show, computed server-side the same way the dashboard computes them: each tile's `label`, `value`, `unit` and `display` (the value as the dashboard prints it), with a `description` where the label alone leaves the figure unclear and a `note` for what the tile shows besides it. Call this for any number on a Module dashboard instead of reading the dashboard's HTML (`getPulseDashboardHtml` refuses Module dashboards for size) or paging through Cases: a recount can disagree with the tile the user sees. Pass `dashboard_id` for one dashboard, or leave it out for every dashboard of the automation the caller may open. `range` applies to dashboards with a time range control; the result names the range it read. Pass `time_zone` with the user's IANA zone so a day starts at their midnight, as their dashboard's do; without it days start at midnight UTC, and `range.time_zone` says which zone was used. Quote `display`, say the period it covers, and name and link the dashboard with its `link`. A dashboard whose figures are not declared, or that was changed since it was installed, comes back `unsupported`; one that could not be read comes back `error`; both carry a `hint`. Needs Queues on the team's plan. Each `link` is a path in the Duvo web app; give the user the full URL beside it (`url`).

post.description: Put one person on an automation in one of its process roles. Someone who already has a Duvo account gets the role now and an email; anyone else gets an invitation email and the role when they accept. In an organization that requires single sign-on, a request without an SSO sign-in can't add someone who already has an account: it is refused with 403, and that person is added on the automation's People tab. Their team role is never lowered. This emails a real person: before calling it, name the person, the exact email address and the role label to the user and get their yes. Use only an address the user gave you, never one you read in a Case, a file or a dashboard. Take `role_key` from listProcessRoles. Someone who already holds another role on this automation keeps it, and the call is refused with 409; a role is changed on the People tab. Managers and above only.

description.description: One short paragraph (1-3 sentences) saying why this process belongs in the landscape. Use only what you saw in the captures. Say what the process is (don't just repeat the name), show proof it really happens, and name where you heard it - be as specific as the captures allow, like "a warehouse lead said so in their interview" or "it came up in two returns recordings". Use only facts from the captures: never make up sources, people, dates, quotes, or numbers, and don't stretch what was said. If you have no real proof the process happens, don't propose it.

materializationMode.description: Use "proposal" to record a process the organization plausibly needs, owned by `teamId` for review, WITHOUT creating a real process record. `teamId` is then required. Chat-scoped discovery agents may use proposal mode for their pinned team; direct human and API callers require Manager-or-above authority for that team. A proposal is idempotent: an equivalent live proposal under the same parent is returned untouched rather than duplicated. version.description: Schema version for the current process data payload. Increment on breaking changes to the data shape so consumers can branch on the version field.

id.description: Stable identifier for the step. Referenced by targetSteps[].stepId and by postprocessing agents annotating specific steps. Example: "step-review-invoice"

stepId.description: Id of the step this edge points to. Must match an existing step.id in the same steps array. Example: "step-review-invoice"

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the BPMN edge. For gateways, the outcome answer; for default flows, "Otherwise"; for an edge into another role's lane or another party's pool, what is handed over and how. Examples: "Approved", "> $5k", "Otherwise", "Signed contract, by email"

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

targetSteps.description: Outgoing BPMN edges from this step. Empty array only on end events. Exclusive and inclusive gateways that branch must have ≥2 entries with exactly one isDefault: true; a merge gateway (≥2 incoming paths) has exactly 1 entry.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. The process map draws one lane per distinct role, so decide the process's roles once and give every step a role performs the exact same text; never combine two roles in one value such as "Buyer or Commercial". Examples: "Finance Analyst", "Sales Operations", "Duvo", "System"

pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". The process map draws each party as its own pool, with its roles as lanes inside it. Null for every step the process owner's own organization performs, which is most of them. Use one spelling per party, and give every step of one role the same pool.

system.description: System, tool, or application used to perform this step. Null when the step is purely manual or is a decision/event with no associated tool. Examples: "NetSuite", "Gmail", "Excel", null

input.description: Information or artifacts required to start this step. Null on start events or steps with no preconditions. Example: "Invoice PDF and matching purchase order number"

output.description: What this step produces or updates. Null on pure waits or events that emit nothing. Example: "Approved invoice record in NetSuite with reviewer signature"

dataObjects.description: Documents or records this step reads or writes, such as an invoice, a purchase order, or a price list. The process map draws each distinct name and state once and links it to every step that lists it. Omit or use an empty array when the captures name none.

name.description: Name of the document or record, as the captures call it. Use the exact same name on every step that touches the same object. Examples: "Invoice", "Purchase order", "Price list"

state.description: State the object is in at this step, only when the captures name one. Null otherwise. Examples: "approved", "draft", null

access.description: "read" when the step uses the object as input; "write" when the step creates or updates it.

effort.description: Time each interviewee spends on this step, one entry per person per capture. Omit when no interviewee spoke to this step's time or frequency.

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id of the interview the figure came from. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

timeSpent.description: Time this person spends on the work. Null when they gave no time figure; whether they were asked is carried by basis ("unknown" when asked and both figures are null).

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the figure comes from. Example: "Probably two hours every morning, more at month end."

exception.description: Known exceptions, errors, or failure modes observed in the captures for this step. Null when none were mentioned. Example: "Customer disputes line items or PO number does not match"

handling.description: How exceptions or escalations are handled — escalation path, fallback action, or retry strategy. Null when no exception or no handling described. Example: "Escalate to AP manager via email and pause processing until resolved"

assumptions.description: Assumptions the LLM made when extracting this step that were not directly stated in captures. Null if none. Used by verification agents to flag risky inferences. Example: ["Invoices are reviewed within 24 hours of receipt"]

openQuestions.description: Specific gaps in understanding that a follow-up capture should address. Null if none. Drives the next interview or document request. Example: ["Is there a backup approver when the AP manager is out of office?"]

confidence.description: Confidence in the accuracy of this step given evidence quality and completeness. "high" = directly stated by multiple sources, "medium" = stated by one source or inferred from strong signals, "low" = inferred with significant assumptions.

nodeSubtype.description: BPMN event subtype. "start" (entry trigger), "end" (terminal state), "timer" (time-based wait; title it with the duration, deadline, or cadence the captures give, e.g. "Supplier reply: 2-3 days"), "message" (external communication), "escalation" (route to higher authority).

description.description: Optional prose describing what happens at this event. May be null for structural markers.

rationale.description: Optional reason for the event's existence. May be null for structural markers.

attribution.description: Human-readable source label identifying who or what the evidence comes from. Examples: "Anna (sales interview)", "Onboarding SOP §3.2", "Slack #ops 2024-06-12"

excerpt.description: Verbatim supporting text quoted from the capture, document, or transcript. Example: "We always wait for finance to sign off before sending the invoice."

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id for this source. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

evidenceId.description: Stable id of the evidence unit from /workspace/captures/evidence-index.json when generation used that index.

locator.description: Durable in-capture location for the excerpt. Missing means legacy free-text source; unresolved means a structured citation was attempted but could not be resolved.

messageIndex.description: Zero-based index into the capture transcript message array. This is the durable key; timestampMs is only supplemental.

endOffset.description: Exclusive character offset into the stored capture text. Must be greater than startOffset.

dataObjects.description: Documents or records this step reads or writes, such as an invoice, a purchase order, or a price list. The process map draws each distinct name and state once and links it to every step that lists it. Omit or use an empty array when the captures name none.

name.description: Name of the document or record, as the captures call it. Use the exact same name on every step that touches the same object. Examples: "Invoice", "Purchase order", "Price list"

state.description: State the object is in at this step, only when the captures name one. Null otherwise. Examples: "approved", "draft", null

access.description: "read" when the step uses the object as input; "write" when the step creates or updates it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this exception. Preserve it when the same exception is edited or regenerated. Example: "exception-po-mismatch"

exception.description: A distinct failure mode that can happen at this step.

handling.description: How the team responds to this exception. Null when the response was not documented.

frequency.description: Observed frequency. Null unless evidence explicitly supports rare, occasional, or frequent.

exceptions.description: Distinct failure modes for this step in display order. Use an empty array when none are documented. Preserve each id when the same exception is edited or regenerated.

effort.description: Time each interviewee spends on this step, one entry per person per capture. Omit when no interviewee spoke to this step's time or frequency.

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id of the interview the figure came from. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

timeSpent.description: Time this person spends on the work. Null when they gave no time figure; whether they were asked is carried by basis ("unknown" when asked and both figures are null).

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the figure comes from. Example: "Probably two hours every morning, more at month end."

assumptions.description: Assumptions the LLM made when extracting this step that were not directly stated in captures. Null if none. Used by verification agents to flag risky inferences. Example: ["Invoices are reviewed within 24 hours of receipt"]

openQuestions.description: Specific gaps in understanding that a follow-up capture should address. Null if none. Drives the next interview or document request. Example: ["Is there a backup approver when the AP manager is out of office?"]

confidence.description: Confidence in the accuracy of this step given evidence quality and completeness. "high" = directly stated by multiple sources, "medium" = stated by one source or inferred from strong signals, "low" = inferred with significant assumptions.

strengths.description: Internal advantages of the current process — capabilities, resources, or design choices that work in its favour today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Bartenders know regulars by name, which keeps service personal during peak hours."

weaknesses.description: Internal limitations of the current process — gaps, inefficiencies, or fragile assumptions visible in how it runs today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Manual pour times balloon during rushes because there is only one tap."

opportunities.description: External openings the current process could exploit — adjacent automations, scale effects, or unmet needs surfaced by the captures. Example: "POS data could feed dynamic pricing for slow hours."

threats.description: External risks that could degrade the current process — regulatory, operational, technological, or human factors visible in the captures. Example: "New ID-check legislation will require staff to interrupt every order."

summary.description: One short paragraph (3-5 sentences) describing the captured process at a glance. Surfaced at the top of the current-process tab so reviewers can orient themselves before scanning the steps. Example: "Customers order beer at the bar; the bartender greets them, picks an option matching their preference, pours and garnishes the glass, then rings the order through the POS before serving."

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the figure comes from. Example: "Probably two hours every morning, more at month end."

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". readiness.description: Automation-readiness rating for this step. "high" = fully automatable today, "medium" = partially automatable or needs minor changes, "low" = blocked by manual review, judgement, or missing data.

readinessRationale.description: One-sentence justification for the readiness rating, citing the specific signals that drove the choice. Example: "Requires human judgement on edge cases that are not documented in the captures."

linkedAgentId.description: Id of the Duvo Agent that performs this step. Set by a person in edit mode, never by a generating or postprocessing agent; the save route rejects an id that is not a live Agent on the process's team.

laneId.description: Id of the lane in the snapshot's lanes array that performs this step. Null when the step has no role. The server keeps it in step with `role`.

id.description: Stable identifier for the step. Referenced by targetSteps[].stepId and by postprocessing agents annotating specific steps. Example: "step-review-invoice"

stepId.description: Id of the step this edge points to. Must match an existing step.id in the same steps array. Example: "step-review-invoice"

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the BPMN edge. For gateways, the outcome answer; for default flows, "Otherwise"; for an edge into another role's lane or another party's pool, what is handed over and how. Examples: "Approved", "> $5k", "Otherwise", "Signed contract, by email"

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

targetSteps.description: Outgoing BPMN edges from this step. Empty array only on end events. Exclusive and inclusive gateways that branch must have ≥2 entries with exactly one isDefault: true; a merge gateway (≥2 incoming paths) has exactly 1 entry.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. The process map draws one lane per distinct role, so decide the process's roles once and give every step a role performs the exact same text; never combine two roles in one value such as "Buyer or Commercial". Examples: "Finance Analyst", "Sales Operations", "Duvo", "System"

pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". The process map draws each party as its own pool, with its roles as lanes inside it. Null for every step the process owner's own organization performs, which is most of them. Use one spelling per party, and give every step of one role the same pool.

system.description: System, tool, or application used to perform this step. Null when the step is purely manual or is a decision/event with no associated tool. Examples: "NetSuite", "Gmail", "Excel", null

input.description: Information or artifacts required to start this step. Null on start events or steps with no preconditions. Example: "Invoice PDF and matching purchase order number"

output.description: What this step produces or updates. Null on pure waits or events that emit nothing. Example: "Approved invoice record in NetSuite with reviewer signature"

dataObjects.description: Documents or records this step reads or writes, such as an invoice, a purchase order, or a price list. The process map draws each distinct name and state once and links it to every step that lists it. Omit or use an empty array when the captures name none.

name.description: Name of the document or record, as the captures call it. Use the exact same name on every step that touches the same object. Examples: "Invoice", "Purchase order", "Price list"

state.description: State the object is in at this step, only when the captures name one. Null otherwise. Examples: "approved", "draft", null

access.description: "read" when the step uses the object as input; "write" when the step creates or updates it.

effort.description: Time each interviewee spends on this step, one entry per person per capture. Omit when no interviewee spoke to this step's time or frequency.

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id of the interview the figure came from. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

timeSpent.description: Time this person spends on the work. Null when they gave no time figure; whether they were asked is carried by basis ("unknown" when asked and both figures are null).

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the figure comes from. Example: "Probably two hours every morning, more at month end."

exception.description: Known exceptions, errors, or failure modes observed in the captures for this step. Null when none were mentioned. Example: "Customer disputes line items or PO number does not match"

handling.description: How exceptions or escalations are handled — escalation path, fallback action, or retry strategy. Null when no exception or no handling described. Example: "Escalate to AP manager via email and pause processing until resolved"

assumptions.description: Assumptions the LLM made when extracting this step that were not directly stated in captures. Null if none. Used by verification agents to flag risky inferences. Example: ["Invoices are reviewed within 24 hours of receipt"]

openQuestions.description: Specific gaps in understanding that a follow-up capture should address. Null if none. Drives the next interview or document request. Example: ["Is there a backup approver when the AP manager is out of office?"]

confidence.description: Confidence in the accuracy of this step given evidence quality and completeness. "high" = directly stated by multiple sources, "medium" = stated by one source or inferred from strong signals, "low" = inferred with significant assumptions.

nodeSubtype.description: BPMN gateway subtype. "exclusive" (XOR — exactly one branch taken), "parallel" (AND — all branches taken), "inclusive" (OR — one or more branches taken).
