mappedVersionIndex.description: Zero-based index in versions of the account represented by this step in the current diagram. Omit when unknown. Update or clear it when the diagram or versions change. This records the diagram content, not a resolved conflict.

attribution.description: Human-readable source label identifying who or what the evidence comes from. Examples: "Anna (sales interview)", "Onboarding SOP §3.2", "Slack #ops 2024-06-12"

excerpt.description: Verbatim supporting text quoted from the capture, document, or transcript. Example: "We always wait for finance to sign off before sending the invoice."

evidenceId.description: Stable id of the evidence unit from /workspace/captures/evidence-index.json when generation used that index.

locator.description: Durable in-capture location for the excerpt. Missing means legacy free-text source; unresolved means a structured citation was attempted but could not be resolved.

messageIndex.description: Zero-based index into the capture transcript message array. This is the durable key; timestampMs is only supplemental.

timestampMs.description: Optional epoch-millisecond timestamp for the transcript message when the capture supplied one.

startOffset.description: Zero-based character offset into the stored capture text.

endOffset.description: Exclusive character offset into the stored capture text. Must be greater than startOffset.

pageNumber.description: Optional one-based PDF page number when the stored capture has page metadata.

startLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text starts on pageNumber.

endLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text ends on pageNumber.

elementId.description: BPMN XML element id within an uploaded .bpmn document.

elementType.description: Optional BPMN element type as parsed from the XML, for example "bpmn:UserTask" or "bpmn:ExclusiveGateway".

name.description: Optional BPMN element name as parsed from the XML. The element id is the durable key.

timestampMs.description: Epoch-millisecond frame timestamp matching a screenshare frame filename.

sourceConfidence.description: Confidence in this individual source citation. "high" = direct quote at the locator, "medium" = strong nearby evidence, "low" = weak or inferred support.

resolutionStatus.description: Resolution status for the structured source link. Legacy sources may omit this field.

title.description: Short heading describing this account; the excerpt remains the exact source quote

id.description: Id of the `clarity_proposal_extra_capture_request` row this slot points at. Created server-side by the agent after the LLM call; the LLM never produces this value.

gap.description: Plain-language description of what about this step is unknown or under-specified, blocking automation. One short sentence. Example: "We don't know which fields the AP analyst copies from the invoice into NetSuite."

proposal.description: What the new capture should include in order to resolve the gap — concrete actions, screens, or decisions the user should walk through. readiness.description: Automation-readiness rating for this step. "high" = fully automatable today, "medium" = partially automatable or needs minor changes, "low" = blocked by manual review, judgement, or missing data.

readinessRationale.description: One-sentence justification for the readiness rating, citing the specific signals that drove the choice. Example: "Requires human judgement on edge cases that are not documented in the captures."

linkedAgentId.description: Id of the Duvo Agent that performs this step. Set by a person in edit mode, never by a generating or postprocessing agent; the save route rejects an id that is not a live Agent on the process's team.

laneId.description: Id of the lane in the snapshot's lanes array that performs this step. Null when the step has no role. The server keeps it in step with `role`.

id.description: Stable identifier for the step. Referenced by targetSteps[].stepId and by postprocessing agents annotating specific steps. Example: "step-review-invoice"

stepId.description: Id of the step this edge points to. Must match an existing step.id in the same steps array. Example: "step-review-invoice"

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the BPMN edge. For gateways, the outcome answer; for default flows, "Otherwise"; for an edge into another role's lane or another party's pool, what is handed over and how. Examples: "Approved", "> $5k", "Otherwise", "Signed contract, by email"

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

targetSteps.description: Outgoing BPMN edges from this step. Empty array only on end events. Exclusive and inclusive gateways that branch must have ≥2 entries with exactly one isDefault: true; a merge gateway (≥2 incoming paths) has exactly 1 entry.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. The process map draws one lane per distinct role, so decide the process's roles once and give every step a role performs the exact same text; never combine two roles in one value such as "Buyer or Commercial". Examples: "Finance Analyst", "Sales Operations", "Duvo", "System"

pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". The process map draws each party as its own pool, with its roles as lanes inside it. Null for every step the process owner's own organization performs, which is most of them. Use one spelling per party, and give every step of one role the same pool.

system.description: System, tool, or application used to perform this step. Null when the step is purely manual or is a decision/event with no associated tool. Examples: "NetSuite", "Gmail", "Excel", null

input.description: Information or artifacts required to start this step. Null on start events or steps with no preconditions. Example: "Invoice PDF and matching purchase order number"

output.description: What this step produces or updates. Null on pure waits or events that emit nothing. Example: "Approved invoice record in NetSuite with reviewer signature"

dataObjects.description: Documents or records this step reads or writes, such as an invoice, a purchase order, or a price list. The process map draws each distinct name and state once and links it to every step that lists it. Omit or use an empty array when the captures name none.

name.description: Name of the document or record, as the captures call it. Use the exact same name on every step that touches the same object. Examples: "Invoice", "Purchase order", "Price list"

state.description: State the object is in at this step, only when the captures name one. Null otherwise. Examples: "approved", "draft", null

access.description: "read" when the step uses the object as input; "write" when the step creates or updates it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this exception. Preserve it when the same exception is edited or regenerated. Example: "exception-po-mismatch"

exception.description: A distinct failure mode that can happen at this step.

handling.description: How the team responds to this exception. Null when the response was not documented.

frequency.description: Observed frequency. Null unless evidence explicitly supports rare, occasional, or frequent.

exceptions.description: Distinct failure modes for this step in display order. Use an empty array when none are documented. Preserve each id when the same exception is edited or regenerated.

effort.description: Time each interviewee spends on this step, one entry per person per capture. Omit when no interviewee spoke to this step's time or frequency.

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id of the interview the figure came from. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

timeSpent.description: Time this person spends on the work. Null when they gave no time figure; whether they were asked is carried by basis ("unknown" when asked and both figures are null).

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the figure comes from. Example: "Probably two hours every morning, more at month end."

assumptions.description: Assumptions the LLM made when extracting this step that were not directly stated in captures. Null if none. Used by verification agents to flag risky inferences. Example: ["Invoices are reviewed within 24 hours of receipt"]

openQuestions.description: Specific gaps in understanding that a follow-up capture should address. Null if none. Drives the next interview or document request. Example: ["Is there a backup approver when the AP manager is out of office?"]

confidence.description: Confidence in the accuracy of this step given evidence quality and completeness. "high" = directly stated by multiple sources, "medium" = stated by one source or inferred from strong signals, "low" = inferred with significant assumptions.

description.description: Full prose paragraph describing what happens in this step in natural language. Used for documentation reconstruction. Example: "Finance reviews the invoice in NetSuite, checking line item accuracy and matching against the purchase order before flagging for approval."

mappedVersionIndex.description: Zero-based index in versions of the account represented by this step in the current diagram. Omit when unknown. Update or clear it when the diagram or versions change. This records the diagram content, not a resolved conflict.

attribution.description: Human-readable source label identifying who or what the evidence comes from. Examples: "Anna (sales interview)", "Onboarding SOP §3.2", "Slack #ops 2024-06-12"

excerpt.description: Verbatim supporting text quoted from the capture, document, or transcript. Example: "We always wait for finance to sign off before sending the invoice."

evidenceId.description: Stable id of the evidence unit from /workspace/captures/evidence-index.json when generation used that index.

locator.description: Durable in-capture location for the excerpt. Missing means legacy free-text source; unresolved means a structured citation was attempted but could not be resolved.

messageIndex.description: Zero-based index into the capture transcript message array. This is the durable key; timestampMs is only supplemental.

timestampMs.description: Optional epoch-millisecond timestamp for the transcript message when the capture supplied one.

startOffset.description: Zero-based character offset into the stored capture text.

endOffset.description: Exclusive character offset into the stored capture text. Must be greater than startOffset.

pageNumber.description: Optional one-based PDF page number when the stored capture has page metadata.

startLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text starts on pageNumber.

endLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text ends on pageNumber.

elementId.description: BPMN XML element id within an uploaded .bpmn document.

elementType.description: Optional BPMN element type as parsed from the XML, for example "bpmn:UserTask" or "bpmn:ExclusiveGateway".

name.description: Optional BPMN element name as parsed from the XML. The element id is the durable key.

timestampMs.description: Epoch-millisecond frame timestamp matching a screenshare frame filename.

sourceConfidence.description: Confidence in this individual source citation. "high" = direct quote at the locator, "medium" = strong nearby evidence, "low" = weak or inferred support.

resolutionStatus.description: Resolution status for the structured source link. Legacy sources may omit this field.

title.description: Short heading describing this account; the excerpt remains the exact source quote

id.description: Id of the `clarity_proposal_extra_capture_request` row this slot points at. Created server-side by the agent after the LLM call; the LLM never produces this value.

gap.description: Plain-language description of what about this step is unknown or under-specified, blocking automation. One short sentence. Example: "We don't know which fields the AP analyst copies from the invoice into NetSuite."

proposal.description: What the new capture should include in order to resolve the gap — concrete actions, screens, or decisions the user should walk through. Optional: omit when no specific proposal can be inferred. Example: "Walk through reviewing one invoice in NetSuite end-to-end while narrating each field you check."

readiness.description: Automation-readiness rating for this step. "high" = fully automatable today, "medium" = partially automatable or needs minor changes, "low" = blocked by manual review, judgement, or missing data.

readinessRationale.description: One-sentence justification for the readiness rating, citing the specific signals that drove the choice. Example: "Requires human judgement on edge cases that are not documented in the captures."

linkedAgentId.description: Id of the Duvo Agent that performs this step. Set by a person in edit mode, never by a generating or postprocessing agent; the save route rejects an id that is not a live Agent on the process's team.

laneId.description: Id of the lane in the snapshot's lanes array that performs this step. Null when the step has no role. The server keeps it in step with `role`.

swot.description: SWOT analysis produced by the swot-analysis postprocessing agent. `undefined` = agent has not yet run; `null` = agent ran and produced no analysis.

strengths.description: Internal advantages of the current process — capabilities, resources, or design choices that work in its favour today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Bartenders know regulars by name, which keeps service personal during peak hours."

weaknesses.description: Internal limitations of the current process — gaps, inefficiencies, or fragile assumptions visible in how it runs today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Manual pour times balloon during rushes because there is only one tap."

opportunities.description: External openings the current process could exploit — adjacent automations, scale effects, or unmet needs surfaced by the captures. Example: "POS data could feed dynamic pricing for slow hours."

threats.description: External risks that could degrade the current process — regulatory, operational, technological, or human factors visible in the captures. Example: "New ID-check legislation will require staff to interrupt every order."

summary.description: One short paragraph (3-5 sentences) describing the captured process at a glance. Surfaced at the top of the current-process tab so reviewers can orient themselves before scanning the steps. Example: "Customers order beer at the bar; the bartender greets them, picks an option matching their preference, pours and garnishes the glass, then rings the order through the POS before serving."

projectedImpact.description: Answer-first, MECE-structured business case. 4-8 sentences of prose + one markdown assumptions table. Null when team context is insufficient to produce any quantitative or qualitative assessment.

lanes.description: Role lanes of the process map, each defined once. Absent on snapshots written before lanes existed; the read model derives them from each step's role.

id.description: Stable identifier for the lane, referenced by each step's laneId. Example: "lane-1"

name.description: The role, team, or system this lane stands for, as the reader sees it in the lane header. Example: "Finance Analyst"

id.description: Snapshot id

parent_id.description: Parent snapshot this row forked from, if any

status.description: Versioning state. Only one 'live' row per process at a time; drafts may be edited or generating before promotion.

creator_type.description: Whether this row was created by a user edit ('human'), an AI pipeline run ('ai'), or a module template's seeded document ('seed'). The value set may grow; see x-extensible-enum.

user_id.description: Creator user id (the human who edited or triggered the run).

sandbox_id.description: E2B sandbox id that produced AI rows; null for user edits.

last_session_id.description: Claude SDK session id for artifact-chat follow-up reuse.

version.description: Schema version for the current process data payload. Increment on breaking changes to the data shape so consumers can branch on the version field.

id.description: Stable identifier for the step. Referenced by targetSteps[].stepId and by postprocessing agents annotating specific steps. Example: "step-review-invoice"

stepId.description: Id of the step this edge points to. Must match an existing step.id in the same steps array. Example: "step-review-invoice"

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the BPMN edge. For gateways, the outcome answer; for default flows, "Otherwise"; for an edge into another role's lane or another party's pool, what is handed over and how. Examples: "Approved", "> $5k", "Otherwise", "Signed contract, by email"

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

targetSteps.description: Outgoing BPMN edges from this step. Empty array only on end events. Exclusive and inclusive gateways that branch must have ≥2 entries with exactly one isDefault: true; a merge gateway (≥2 incoming paths) has exactly 1 entry.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. The process map draws one lane per distinct role, so decide the process's roles once and give every step a role performs the exact same text; never combine two roles in one value such as "Buyer or Commercial". Examples: "Finance Analyst", "Sales Operations", "Duvo", "System"

pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". The process map draws each party as its own pool, with its roles as lanes inside it. Null for every step the process owner's own organization performs, which is most of them. Use one spelling per party, and give every step of one role the same pool.

system.description: System, tool, or application used to perform this step. Null when the step is purely manual or is a decision/event with no associated tool. Examples: "NetSuite", "Gmail", "Excel", null

input.description: Information or artifacts required to start this step. Null on start events or steps with no preconditions. Example: "Invoice PDF and matching purchase order number"

output.description: What this step produces or updates. Null on pure waits or events that emit nothing. Example: "Approved invoice record in NetSuite with reviewer signature"

dataObjects.description: Documents or records this step reads or writes, such as an invoice, a purchase order, or a price list. The process map draws each distinct name and state once and links it to every step that lists it. Omit or use an empty array when the captures name none.

name.description: Name of the document or record, as the captures call it. Use the exact same name on every step that touches the same object. Examples: "Invoice", "Purchase order", "Price list"

state.description: State the object is in at this step, only when the captures name one. Null otherwise. Examples: "approved", "draft", null

access.description: "read" when the step uses the object as input; "write" when the step creates or updates it.

effort.description: Time each interviewee spends on this step, one entry per person per capture. Omit when no interviewee spoke to this step's time or frequency.

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id of the interview the figure came from. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

timeSpent.description: Time this person spends on the work. Null when they gave no time figure; whether they were asked is carried by basis ("unknown" when asked and both figures are null).

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the figure comes from. Example: "Probably two hours every morning, more at month end."

exception.description: Known exceptions, errors, or failure modes observed in the captures for this step. Null when none were mentioned. Example: "Customer disputes line items or PO number does not match"

handling.description: How exceptions or escalations are handled — escalation path, fallback action, or retry strategy. Null when no exception or no handling described. Example: "Escalate to AP manager via email and pause processing until resolved"

assumptions.description: Assumptions the LLM made when extracting this step that were not directly stated in captures. Null if none. Used by verification agents to flag risky inferences. Example: ["Invoices are reviewed within 24 hours of receipt"]

openQuestions.description: Specific gaps in understanding that a follow-up capture should address. Null if none. Drives the next interview or document request. Example: ["Is there a backup approver when the AP manager is out of office?"]

confidence.description: Confidence in the accuracy of this step given evidence quality and completeness. "high" = directly stated by multiple sources, "medium" = stated by one source or inferred from strong signals, "low" = inferred with significant assumptions.

nodeSubtype.description: BPMN event subtype. label.description: Human-readable label shown on the BPMN edge. For gateways, the outcome answer; for default flows, "Otherwise"; for an edge into another role's lane or another party's pool, what is handed over and how. Examples: "Approved", "> $5k", "Otherwise", "Signed contract, by email"

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". gap.description: Plain-language description of what about this step is unknown or under-specified, blocking automation. One short sentence. Example: "We don't know which fields the AP analyst copies from the invoice into NetSuite."

readiness.description: Automation-readiness rating for this step. "high" = fully automatable today, "medium" = partially automatable or needs minor changes, "low" = blocked by manual review, judgement, or missing data.

readinessRationale.description: One-sentence justification for the readiness rating, citing the specific signals that drove the choice. Example: "Requires human judgement on edge cases that are not documented in the captures."

linkedAgentId.description: Id of the Duvo Agent that performs this step. Set by a person in edit mode, never by a generating or postprocessing agent; the save route rejects an id that is not a live Agent on the process's team.

laneId.description: Id of the lane in the snapshot's lanes array that performs this step. Null when the step has no role. The server keeps it in step with `role`.

steps.description: Ordered steps describing the proposed redesigned process. Same shape as the current process steps; BPMN topology is encoded by each step's targetSteps[] edges.

summary.description: One short paragraph (3-5 sentences) describing the proposed transformed process at a glance. Surfaced at the top of the transformation-proposal tab so reviewers can orient themselves before scanning the steps. Example: "Customers self-order on a tablet at the bar; a smart tap auto-pours the chosen beer into a labelled glass, which the customer collects from the pickup counter once payment clears."

projectedImpact.description: Answer-first, MECE-structured business case. 4-8 sentences of prose + one markdown assumptions table. Null when team context is insufficient to produce any quantitative or qualitative assessment.

lanes.description: Role lanes of the process map, each defined once. Absent on snapshots written before lanes existed; the read model derives them from each step's role.

id.description: Stable identifier for the lane, referenced by each step's laneId. Example: "lane-1"

name.description: The role, team, or system this lane stands for, as the reader sees it in the lane header. Example: "Finance Analyst"

id.description: Stable identifier for the step. Referenced by targetSteps[].stepId and by postprocessing agents annotating specific steps. Example: "step-review-invoice"

stepId.description: Id of the step this edge points to. Must match an existing step.id in the same steps array. Example: "step-review-invoice"

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the BPMN edge. For gateways, the outcome answer; for default flows, "Otherwise"; for an edge into another role's lane or another party's pool, what is handed over and how. Examples: "Approved", "> $5k", "Otherwise", "Signed contract, by email"

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

targetSteps.description: Outgoing BPMN edges from this step. Empty array only on end events. Exclusive and inclusive gateways that branch must have ≥2 entries with exactly one isDefault: true; a merge gateway (≥2 incoming paths) has exactly 1 entry.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. The process map draws one lane per distinct role, so decide the process's roles once and give every step a role performs the exact same text; never combine two roles in one value such as "Buyer or Commercial". Examples: "Finance Analyst", "Sales Operations", "Duvo", "System"

pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". The process map draws each party as its own pool, with its roles as lanes inside it. Null for every step the process owner's own organization performs, which is most of them. Use one spelling per party, and give every step of one role the same pool.

system.description: System, tool, or application used to perform this step. Null when the step is purely manual or is a decision/event with no associated tool. Examples: "NetSuite", "Gmail", "Excel", null

input.description: Information or artifacts required to start this step. Null on start events or steps with no preconditions. Example: "Invoice PDF and matching purchase order number"

output.description: What this step produces or updates. Null on pure waits or events that emit nothing. Example: "Approved invoice record in NetSuite with reviewer signature"

dataObjects.description: Documents or records this step reads or writes, such as an invoice, a purchase order, or a price list. The process map draws each distinct name and state once and links it to every step that lists it. Omit or use an empty array when the captures name none.

name.description: Name of the document or record, as the captures call it. Use the exact same name on every step that touches the same object. Examples: "Invoice", "Purchase order", "Price list"

state.description: State the object is in at this step, only when the captures name one. Null otherwise. Examples: "approved", "draft", null

access.description: "read" when the step uses the object as input; "write" when the step creates or updates it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this exception. Preserve it when the same exception is edited or regenerated. Example: "exception-po-mismatch"

exception.description: A distinct failure mode that can happen at this step.

handling.description: How the team responds to this exception. Null when the response was not documented.

frequency.description: Observed frequency. Null unless evidence explicitly supports rare, occasional, or frequent.

exceptions.description: Distinct failure modes for this step in display order. Use an empty array when none are documented. Preserve each id when the same exception is edited or regenerated.

effort.description: Time each interviewee spends on this step, one entry per person per capture. Omit when no interviewee spoke to this step's time or frequency.

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

timeSpent.description: Time this person spends on the work. Null when they gave no time figure; whether they were asked is carried by basis ("unknown" when asked and both figures are null).

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

linkedAgentId.description: Id of the Duvo Agent that performs this step. Set by a person in edit mode, never by a generating or postprocessing agent; the save route rejects an id that is not a live Agent on the process's team.

laneId.description: Id of the lane in the snapshot's lanes array that performs this step. Null when the step has no role. The server keeps it in step with `role`.

id.description: Stable identifier for the step. Referenced by targetSteps[].stepId and by postprocessing agents annotating specific steps. Example: "step-review-invoice"

stepId.description: Id of the step this edge points to. Must match an existing step.id in the same steps array. Example: "step-review-invoice"

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the BPMN edge. For gateways, the outcome answer; for default flows, "Otherwise"; for an edge into another role's lane or another party's pool, what is handed over and how. Examples: "Approved", "> $5k", "Otherwise", "Signed contract, by email"

isDefault.description: True on exactly one outgoing edge of a branching exclusive or inclusive gateway, marking the fallback taken when no other condition matches. False on all other edges, including the single edge leaving a merge gateway.

targetSteps.description: Outgoing BPMN edges from this step. Empty array only on end events. Exclusive and inclusive gateways that branch must have ≥2 entries with exactly one isDefault: true; a merge gateway (≥2 incoming paths) has exactly 1 entry.

title.description: Required node label used in lists and BPMN node labels. Structural markers use defaults such as "Start" and "End".

action.description: Verb-led one-liner summarizing the concrete action performed. Example: "Reviews invoice line items in NetSuite against the purchase order."

role.description: Performer of this step — the specific job title, team, or system. Use "Duvo" for automated actions and "System" for system-triggered steps. The process map draws one lane per distinct role, so decide the process's roles once and give every step a role performs the exact same text; never combine two roles in one value such as "Buyer or Commercial". Examples: "Finance Analyst", "Sales Operations", "Duvo", "System"

pool.description: The organization or party outside the process owner's own organization that performs this step, such as "Supplier", "Customer", "Bank", or "Tax authority". The process map draws each party as its own pool, with its roles as lanes inside it. Null for every step the process owner's own organization performs, which is most of them. Use one spelling per party, and give every step of one role the same pool.

system.description: System, tool, or application used to perform this step. Null when the step is purely manual or is a decision/event with no associated tool. Examples: "NetSuite", "Gmail", "Excel", null

input.description: Information or artifacts required to start this step. Null on start events or steps with no preconditions. Example: "Invoice PDF and matching purchase order number"

output.description: What this step produces or updates. Null on pure waits or events that emit nothing. Example: "Approved invoice record in NetSuite with reviewer signature"

dataObjects.description: Documents or records this step reads or writes, such as an invoice, a purchase order, or a price list. The process map draws each distinct name and state once and links it to every step that lists it. Omit or use an empty array when the captures name none.

name.description: Name of the document or record, as the captures call it. Use the exact same name on every step that touches the same object. Examples: "Invoice", "Purchase order", "Price list"

state.description: State the object is in at this step, only when the captures name one. Null otherwise. Examples: "approved", "draft", null

access.description: "read" when the step uses the object as input; "write" when the step creates or updates it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this exception. Preserve it when the same exception is edited or regenerated. Example: "exception-po-mismatch"

exception.description: A distinct failure mode that can happen at this step.

handling.description: How the team responds to this exception. Null when the response was not documented.

frequency.description: Observed frequency. Null unless evidence explicitly supports rare, occasional, or frequent.

exceptions.description: Distinct failure modes for this step in display order. Use an empty array when none are documented. Preserve each id when the same exception is edited or regenerated.

effort.description: Time each interviewee spends on this step, one entry per person per capture. Omit when no interviewee spoke to this step's time or frequency.

person.description: Who reported this effort, matching the source attribution. Example: "Anna, AP Clerk"

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id of the interview the figure came from. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

timeSpent.description: Time this person spends on the work. Null when they gave no time figure; whether they were asked is carried by basis ("unknown" when asked and both figures are null).

hours.description: Hours this person spends on the work per period. Use one best value; for a range ("1 to 2 hours") use the midpoint and keep the range in excerpt. Example: 2

frequency.description: How often the work happens for this person. Null unless they gave a count.

count.description: How many times the work happens per period. Example: 40

basis.description: "stated" = the person gave the number; "estimated" = they gave or accepted a rough guess when pressed; "unknown" = they were asked but gave no figure, so timeSpent and frequency are both null.

excerpt.description: Verbatim quote the figure comes from. Example: "Probably two hours every morning, more at month end."

assumptions.description: Assumptions the LLM made when extracting this step that were not directly stated in captures. Null if none. Used by verification agents to flag risky inferences. Example: ["Invoices are reviewed within 24 hours of receipt"]

openQuestions.description: Specific gaps in understanding that a follow-up capture should address. Null if none. Drives the next interview or document request. Example: ["Is there a backup approver when the AP manager is out of office?"]

confidence.description: Confidence in the accuracy of this step given evidence quality and completeness. "high" = directly stated by multiple sources, "medium" = stated by one source or inferred from strong signals, "low" = inferred with significant assumptions.

nodeSubtype.description: BPMN gateway subtype. "exclusive" (XOR — exactly one branch taken), "parallel" (AND — all branches taken), "inclusive" (OR — one or more branches taken).

description.description: Full prose describing the decision logic at this gateway.

rationale.description: Why this branching decision exists in the process.

attribution.description: Human-readable source label identifying who or what the evidence comes from. Examples: "Anna (sales interview)", "Onboarding SOP §3.2", "Slack #ops 2024-06-12"

excerpt.description: Verbatim supporting text quoted from the capture, document, or transcript. Example: "We always wait for finance to sign off before sending the invoice."

captureId.description: Durable clarity_capture id for this source. Use app-owned ids from the evidence index, never sandbox file paths.

evidenceId.description: Stable id of the evidence unit from /workspace/captures/evidence-index.json when generation used that index.

locator.description: Durable in-capture location for the excerpt. Missing means legacy free-text source; unresolved means a structured citation was attempted but could not be resolved.

messageIndex.description: Zero-based index into the capture transcript message array. This is the durable key; timestampMs is only supplemental.

timestampMs.description: Optional epoch-millisecond timestamp for the transcript message when the capture supplied one.

startOffset.description: Zero-based character offset into the stored capture text.

endOffset.description: Exclusive character offset into the stored capture text. Must be greater than startOffset.

pageNumber.description: Optional one-based PDF page number when the stored capture has page metadata.

startLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text starts on pageNumber.

endLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text ends on pageNumber.

elementId.description: BPMN XML element id within an uploaded .bpmn document.

elementType.description: Optional BPMN element type as parsed from the XML, for example "bpmn:UserTask" or "bpmn:ExclusiveGateway".

name.description: Optional BPMN element name as parsed from the XML. The element id is the durable key.

timestampMs.description: Epoch-millisecond frame timestamp matching a screenshare frame filename.

sourceConfidence.description: Confidence in this individual source citation. "high" = direct quote at the locator, "medium" = strong nearby evidence, "low" = weak or inferred support.

resolutionStatus.description: Resolution status for the structured source link. Legacy sources may omit this field.

sources.description: Evidence supporting the decision criteria.

condition.description: Decision criteria evaluated at this gateway. BPMN requires this on every branching gateway. Existing rows persisted with null/empty values parse as "unknown" via a read-side preprocess; producers should write a real condition string going forward.

mappedVersionIndex.description: Zero-based index in versions of the account represented by this step in the current diagram. Omit when unknown. Update or clear it when the diagram or versions change. This records the diagram content, not a resolved conflict.

evidenceId.description: Stable id of the evidence unit from /workspace/captures/evidence-index.json when generation used that index.

timestampMs.description: Optional epoch-millisecond timestamp for the transcript message when the capture supplied one.

endOffset.description: Exclusive character offset into the stored capture text. Must be greater than startOffset.

startLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text starts on pageNumber.

endLine.description: Optional one-based line number where the cited text ends on pageNumber.

name.description: Optional BPMN element name as parsed from the XML. The element id is the durable key.

resolutionStatus.description: Resolution status for the structured source link. Legacy sources may omit this field.

title.description: Short heading describing this account; the excerpt remains the exact source quote

id.description: Id of the `clarity_proposal_extra_capture_request` row this slot points at. Created server-side by the agent after the LLM call; the LLM never produces this value.

gap.description: Plain-language description of what about this step is unknown or under-specified, blocking automation. One short sentence. Example: "We don't know which fields the AP analyst copies from the invoice into NetSuite."

proposal.description: What the new capture should include in order to resolve the gap — concrete actions, screens, or decisions the user should walk through. Optional: omit when no specific proposal can be inferred. Example: "Walk through reviewing one invoice in NetSuite end-to-end while narrating each field you check."

id.description: Id of the `clarity_proposal_extra_capture_request` row this slot points at. Created server-side by the agent after the LLM call; the LLM never produces this value.

Optional: omit when no specific proposal can be inferred. Example: "Walk through reviewing one invoice in NetSuite end-to-end while narrating each field you check."

readiness.description: Automation-readiness rating for this step. "high" = fully automatable today, "medium" = partially automatable or needs minor changes, "low" = blocked by manual review, judgement, or missing data.

readinessRationale.description: One-sentence justification for the readiness rating, citing the specific signals that drove the choice. Example: "Requires human judgement on edge cases that are not documented in the captures."

laneId.description: Id of the lane in the snapshot's lanes array that performs this step. Null when the step has no role. The server keeps it in step with `role`.

summary.description: One short paragraph (3-5 sentences) describing the proposed transformed process at a glance. Surfaced at the top of the transformation-proposal tab so reviewers can orient themselves before scanning the steps. Example: "Customers self-order on a tablet at the bar; a smart tap auto-pours the chosen beer into a labelled glass, which the customer collects from the pickup counter once payment clears."

projectedImpact.description: Answer-first, MECE-structured business case. 4-8 sentences of prose + one markdown assumptions table. Null when team context is insufficient to produce any quantitative or qualitative assessment.

lanes.description: Role lanes of the process map, each defined once. Absent on snapshots written before lanes existed; the read model derives them from each step's role.

id.description: Stable identifier for the lane, referenced by each step's laneId. Example: "lane-1"

name.description: The role, team, or system this lane stands for, as the reader sees it in the lane header. Example: "Finance Analyst"

data.description: Opaque BPMN payload for the proposed transformed process.

post.description: Trigger a snapshot generation pipeline for a v2 clarity process, selected by kind. `current_process` runs the generateCurrentProcess pipeline (body fields are proposal-only and rejected); `transformation_proposal` runs the generate or regenerate proposal pipeline. Returns 202 immediately and finalises asynchronously via the cc-server webhook stream.

source_snapshot_id.description: Automation proposals only: id of the current-process snapshot to anchor the new proposal to. Defaults to the latest snapshot for the process.

regenerate_from.description: Automation proposals only: id of a prior proposal snapshot to refine. When supplied, runs the regenerate pipeline using that proposal's current-process snapshot as the anchor and the extra captures collected since.

custom_guidance.description: Automation proposals only: optional freeform guidance for this generation. Used as high-priority design guidance, not source-of-truth evidence.

transformation_aggressiveness.description: Transformation proposals only: the transformation appetite. `aggressive`, `conservative`, and `none` redesign around Duvo automation with decreasing freedom to change the process; `optimize` standardizes and streamlines the process while every step stays performed by people.

post.description: Stop an in-flight snapshot generation for the selected kind. Reads the sandbox id from the process row, kills the sandbox, flips the process back to `review`, and clears the sandbox marker so any late webhook from the killed run is dropped as stale.

Set up the user's Duvo workspace, or return the one they already have (`created: false`, nothing created). Call it first when the user has no workspace: other tools fail with 'User has no current team' until one exists. A new workspace is on the Free plan, with Clarity and Automation. `has_clarity_access` says whether the team's plan includes Clarity, `interviews_remaining` counts interviews left on the plan without subtracting people invited but not yet interviewed, and `billing_url` is where the user upgrades. If the user's organization or email domain is already on Duvo, the call is refused with a link the user must open.

Invite a person to an organization you administer, optionally assigning them to a team in that organization. Requires an organization Admin, Executive, or Owner role. You cannot grant a role higher than your own.

frontendUrl.description: Deprecated. Use `sendEmail` instead. Kept because its presence is the legacy opt-in for sending the invitation email; the value never sets the link host, which is always the server's configured frontend URL.

sendEmail.description: Email the invitation to the recipient. `false` always suppresses the email. When omitted, the legacy opt-in applies instead: the email is sent only if the deprecated `frontendUrl` is present. Omit both to create the invitation without notifying anyone.

get.description: List teams belonging to an organization you are a member of, including your membership and role in each.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of teams per page (1-100, default 50)

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Filter teams by name (case-insensitive substring match)

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description: Sort order: createdAt (newest first, default) or name (alphabetical)

post.description: Create a new team under an organization you administer. Requires an organization Admin, Executive, or Owner role.

get.description: List every agent across all teams in an organization, with the team it belongs to, the state of its most recent run and the state of its schedules. Intended for external monitoring: it answers 'which agents have gone silent' and 'which agents were switched off' without a request per team or per agent. Requires an organization Admin, Executive, or Owner role, and an API key scoped to all teams you can access — a key pinned to a single team is rejected, because this endpoint spans every team in the organization.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of agents per page (1-100, default 20)

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Filter to agents on this team

parameters.name: schedule_enabled
parameters.description: If true, only agents with at least one enabled schedule; if false, only agents with none (including agents that are never scheduled)

parameters.name: auto_disabled
parameters.description: If true, only agents whose schedule was switched off automatically (e.g. after repeated missing-connection failures); if false, only agents with no auto-disabled schedule

id.description: Unique agent identifier

name.description: Human-readable agent name

team_id.description: Identifier of the team the agent belongs to

team_name.description: Name of the team the agent belongs to

last_run_at.description: ISO 8601 creation timestamp of the agent's most recent run, or null when it has never run

last_run_status.description: Status of the agent's most recent run, or null if it never ran

schedule_enabled.description: Whether at least one of the agent's schedules is enabled

auto_disabled_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which a schedule was switched off automatically, or null when none was

auto_disabled_reason.description: Why a schedule was switched off automatically, when it was

total.description: Total agents matching the filters, ignoring pagination

get.description: List runs across every team in an organization, filtered by status, agent, team, source, evaluation issues and time. Intended for external monitoring: one call covers the whole org instead of one per team. Requires an organization Admin, Executive, or Owner role, and an API key scoped to all teams you can access — a key pinned to a single team is rejected, because this endpoint spans every team in the organization.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of runs per page (1-500, default 20). The cap is higher than the team runs endpoint's because this route serves bulk export: at 100 requests a minute per key, page size is what bounds how fast a month of runs can be pulled.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Resume after the run a previous page ended on: pass the `next_cursor` that page returned, with the same filters and sort_order. Runs created or resolved in between cannot shift a boundary you have already passed, so a sweep sees every run exactly once, and a sweep that started under the default 7-day window keeps that window on every page. This list has no offset parameter: skipping rows costs the database every skipped row, and a run created between two requests shifts every later offset by one, so an offset sweep can repeat or miss a run. 400 when the value is not a cursor this endpoint issued.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter to runs with this status. `needs_attention` is the monitoring status: runs that are waiting on a human or failed, plus runs whose latest evaluation flagged a critical issue — a run can finish as `completed` and still have accomplished nothing.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: Filter to runs on this team

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Filter to runs for this agent

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter to runs created from this source (e.g. api, scheduling)

parameters.name: has_issues
parameters.description: Filter on the run's latest successful evaluation: true returns only runs it flagged, false only runs it did not. Only the latest evaluation counts — an older flag does not match — and a run whose latest evaluation errored, or that has none, counts as unflagged. Omit to return both.

parameters.name: issue_severity
parameters.description: Only runs whose latest successful evaluation has at least one failing rubric at this severity (critical | medium | low). Implies has_issues.

parameters.name: created_after
parameters.description: Return runs created at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Every run has a creation time, so this is the window that returns all runs in a period whatever state they reached — unlike the started and completed windows below, which exclude runs that never started and runs still in flight respectively. When the request carries no lower time bound (`created_after`, `started_after`, `completed_after` or `since`), this defaults to 7 days ago and `default_window_applied` is true in the response: an organization's run history is unbounded, and a monitor wants what is recent. An upper bound alone keeps the default floor. Pass any lower bound to replace it.

parameters.name: created_before
parameters.description: Return runs created before this ISO-8601 timestamp (exclusive). Pair with `created_after` for a period. A closed creation window is also the stable one to paginate: results are ordered by creation time, so runs arriving mid-sweep cannot shift a closed window's pages.

parameters.name: started_after
parameters.description: Return runs that started at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Runs that never started are excluded. Pair with `started_before` to bound a stuck-run query to a window — without a lower bound, `status=running` also counts every run left running months ago.

parameters.name: started_before
parameters.description: Return runs that started before this ISO-8601 timestamp. Combine with status=running to find stuck runs — `since`/`until` filter on completion, so they never match a run that is still going.

parameters.name: completed_after
parameters.description: Return runs completed at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Runs that have not completed are excluded, including every stuck one — reach for `started_after`/`started_before` to bound those. Alias of `since`; pass one or the other, not both.

parameters.name: completed_before
parameters.description: Return runs completed before this ISO-8601 timestamp (exclusive). Runs that have not completed are excluded. Alias of `until`; pass one or the other, not both.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Alias of `completed_after`, kept because it is the name the public team runs endpoint ships. Prefer `completed_after`: this endpoint carries a creation and a start window too, and only the column-named pair says which one this is.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Alias of `completed_before`, kept because it is the name the public team runs endpoint ships. Prefer `completed_before`.

parameters.name: count_only
parameters.description: Skip row selection and enrichment. The normal list response shape is returned with an empty row array and the matching total.

parameters.name: include_total
parameters.description: Return `total`, the count of every matching run ignoring pagination. Off by default: counting walks every match where the page stops at `limit`, so on a large organization it costs orders of magnitude more than the rows themselves. Ask for it when you are driving a pager, not when you are polling. Implied by `count_only`.

id.description: Unique run identifier

status.description: Current run status

team_id.description: Team that owns the run. This is the run's own team, which a cross-team transfer pins to the source team — so it is not always the team the agent belongs to now.

team_name.description: Name of that team, or null when the team no longer exists — a run stays pinned to the team that owned it, and that team can since have been deleted.

user_id.description: User the run belongs to, if any

total.description: Total runs matching the filters, ignoring pagination. Null unless `include_total=true` or `count_only=true` — null means not requested, distinct from a count of 0.

has_more.description: Whether another page exists past this one, determined by looking one row ahead rather than inferred from a full page. False on a count_only response.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` (same filters, same sort_order) to fetch the next page. Null when `has_more` is false. Exact continuation from the last run on this page, unaffected by runs created or resolved in the meantime.

created_after.description: The creation lower bound the query ran with, as ISO 8601: the caller's `created_after`, or 7 days ago when the request carried no time bound at all. Null when the caller bounded the query on another timestamp only.

default_window_applied.description: True when the request carried no time bound and the 7-day creation window was applied for it. A caller that meant "everything" should pass an explicit `created_after`.

get.description: Get org-wide headline insight KPIs (run totals, success rate, distinct active agents and users) aggregated across every team in the organization. Requires an organization Admin, Executive, or Owner role.

parameters.name: endDate

completed_runs.description: Runs that finished with completed status

failed_runs.description: Runs that finished with failed status

success_rate.description: completed_runs / (completed_runs + failed_runs), null when no runs finished in the window

active_agents.description: Distinct agents with at least one run in the window (org-wide, includes since-deleted agents so totals reconcile with run counts)

active_users.description: Distinct users who started at least one run in the window, deduplicated across teams

truncated.description: True when the org has more teams than the aggregation limit — figures cover only the first teams up to the cap

aggregated_teams.description: Number of teams actually included in the aggregation

total_teams.description: Actual team count on the org, even when truncated

Narrow it with `rootId` (one subtree), `ownerTeamId` (one owning team), and `userId` or `search` (one person) — an unfiltered organization roster is large enough to be refused by response-size caps. To find the processes where one person has not captured yet, filter to that person and read `captureCount` per row. `truncated` is true when the node subtree or any single process roster was capped.

post.description: Declare a queue's first Case schema by hand, so a person can type a queue up front instead of waiting for its producing agent to declare the shape. name.description: A human-readable name for the Case schema (1–100 characters).

schema.description: A JSON Schema 2020-12 subset. The root must have type "object"; every object schema, including nested objects, must set additionalProperties to false or the request fails with 400 "Object schemas must set additionalProperties to false". Allowed types: object, array, string, number, integer, boolean, null. Allowed keywords: $schema, $defs, $ref, type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, description, format, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems. Allowed formats: date, date-time, email, uuid. Property names must match /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$/, and every array needs items. Schemas are limited to 65,536 bytes, 16 nested levels, and 256 declared or expanded fields; case JSON payloads are limited to 8 MiB and 10,000 items per array. Minimal valid example: {"type":"object","additionalProperties":false,"properties":{}}.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of cases per page (1-100, default 20).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by one or more status buckets (comma-separated). Values: all, pending, processing, needs_input, postponed, needs_review, resolved, canceled. `processing` covers both a case actively being worked and one waiting on its evaluation.

parameters.description: Filter by highest failing rubric severity (comma-separated). Values: critical, medium. parameters.name: sort_by

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: Filter on a field of a typed queue's json_data, as <path>:<operator>[:<value>] (e.g. $.invoice.amount:gte:5000). Repeat the param to require several; all must match, so two comparisons on one path express a range. Operators: equals, notEquals, in, notIn, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains, isSet, isNotSet. in/notIn take a comma-separated list; isSet/isNotSet take no value. A value is typed by shape (5000 is a number, true a boolean, 00123 a string so a leading zero survives). A path the queue's Case schema does not declare is rejected rather than ignored.

parameters.description: Skip row selection and enrichment. The normal list response shape is returned with an empty row array and the matching total.

post.description: Create one or more cases in a queue. Provide either a single `case` object or a `cases` array (1-100); providing both returns 400. Each case takes a title (max 500 chars), optional labels that will be assigned to the case on creation (missing labels are created on the queue), and an optional priority (`none`, `medium`, or `high`; `medium`/`high` raise it above the default in the queue, `none` is the default; priority only affects the order pending cases are picked up in: due postponed cases are handled first, then higher priority). A guarded queue that has no schema yet accepts free-text `data` only when typed Case schemas are off for that queue — the team has them turned off AND the queue is not inside an automation (there is then no way to declare a schema, so the guard cannot apply). patch.description: Set one or more fields of a typed case's structured `json_data` payload in one atomic write, leaving every other field as stored. Prefer this over `PATCH /cases/{case_id}` with a full `json_data` object when changing some fields: the write reads and locks the latest payload in the database, so a concurrent edit to another field, or to another item of the same array, is preserved. Each `set` entry names a `path`, a JSONPath declared in the queue's current Case schema, and the `value` to store there. A path is dotted object fields (`$.invoice.amount`) with optional array indices in brackets (`$.lines[0]` for a whole item, `$.lines[0].amount` for one field of it). An index must name an item that already exists; an out-of-range index or a non-array parent is refused, and a write never adds or removes items. A `value` can be any JSON value, including an object for an object field. Paths must be distinct, and no path may sit inside another in the same request (`$.lines` beside `$.lines[0]`, or `$.lines[0]` beside `$.lines[0].amount`). An index names a position, so when the array can change between your read and your write, add `expect` entries that pin the item, such as its id field (`$.lines[0].id`): if any stored value differs, nothing is written and the response is a 409. The resulting payload is validated against the queue's current Case schema and the case is re-pinned to that schema version; if any entry is refused, nothing is written. A case without a structured payload yet must be given one with `PATCH /cases/{case_id}` first. Returns the updated case with its event history and approval batches.

expect.description: Preconditions checked against the latest stored payload before any field is set (up to 100). If one does not match, nothing is written and the response is a 409. Use them to make sure an array index still names the item you read.

path.description: JSONPath of a stored value to check, in the same form as a `set` path (e.g. `$.lines[0].id`). Must be declared in the queue's current Case schema.

post.description: Update the status of multiple cases to pending, completed, failed, or canceled. Interrupts any active runs and releases their case ownership, but never cancels their human-in-the-loop state — pending requests and open approval batches stay answerable/resolvable from the run view. Settling a case archives the pending requests on every run attached to it, both the runs this call interrupted and any that were already terminal, so they leave the activity inbox instead of outliving the case there. Resetting to pending archives nothing and re-dispatches cases to the queue's trigger consumer.

get.description: List a queue's active case-level evaluation rubrics — the Pass/Fail questions a whole case is judged against at settlement. Shows the queue's current version's set (auto-generated from the connected Assignments' AOPs, plus any manually-authored rubrics).

post.description: Add one case-level evaluation rubric to a queue's current rubric set. Case-level rubrics judge the whole case (across every Run that touched it) as a Pass/Fail question at settlement. The rubric is added to the queue's current version (build-set) — the set new cases are judged against; a queue only gets one after its first Agent-processed case settles, so this fails with 409 before then, and once the version holds 12 rubrics by default (25 on teams with the newer rubric generator enabled); the error message states the ceiling.

put.description: Replace the entire case-level evaluation rubric set on a queue's current version (1 to N rubrics, N being 12 by default and 25 on teams with the newer rubric generator enabled). Existing rubrics are removed and the supplied list becomes the new set. An empty list is refused — whole-case evaluation regenerates rubrics for an empty set at the next settlement, so a cleared set would not stay cleared; remove individual rubrics instead. Targets the queue's current version (build-set), which exists once its first Agent-processed case settles — this fails with 409 before then. Cases already judged keep their original verdicts.

description.description: A 1-2 sentence Pass condition phrased as a question.

delete.description: Remove a single case-level evaluation rubric. Cases settled after this are no longer judged against it; already-judged cases keep their original verdicts. post.description: Search cases in a queue with rich filters (multi-status, date ranges, label-based filters, and field-value filters over a typed queue's json_data). Use this when the simple query-string filters on GET /v2/queues/:queue_id/cases aren't enough. Each json_data entry is {path, operator, value} where path is a declared scalar in JSONPath dotted form ($.invoice.amount); entries are ANDed, so two comparisons on one path express a range. A path the queue's Case schema does not declare is rejected rather than ignored, as is a value that does not match the field's declared type. The contains operator is case-sensitive (unlike the free-text search parameter). Set count_only=true to skip Case row selection, enrichment, and transformation. The normal response shape is returned with cases: [] and the matching total.

Automations reuse the team's existing agent_folder tree rather than a parallel one, so a converted team keeps the grouping it already had. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason is_setting_up is: the client parses this response, and a backend that predates the column must not throw and take the automation's name down with it.

pinned_at.description: When the calling user pinned this automation to the top of their Automations list, or null when they have not. A pin is per user, like an Agent pin: teammates each keep their own. Defaulted rather than required for the same reason folder_id is.

is_setting_up.description: True while this Module automation's setup is under way. setup_started_at is stamped when the team starts setting up (and again by reopen-setup) and cleared when setup finishes, so this reads as currently in setup, not as a record of a past one. Read together with is_demo, which lives on the detail response: both true is a demo with a build under way; is_demo alone is a demo nobody has begun. On the summary rather than the detail so that a client holding only a list, create or patch response knows the state too, and so every write onto the shared automation collection carries it. Defaulted rather than required: the client parses this response, so a backend that predates the column must not throw and take the automation's name down with it, and nothing on the wire has always meant an automation nobody has set up.

setup_step.description: The key of the latest confirmed setup step, null until Start Setup is pressed. The server only ever advances it forward, so reopening a setup can resume where the team got to. Cleared with the rest of the setup state when setup finishes.

setup_build_chat_id.description: The Ask Duvo chat building the automation from the approved proposal, or null while setup has not reached the build. Not a hard reference: the chat can be deleted while this still names it, which the client reads as no build yet.

setup_progress.description: The setup facts behind the tile's Setup badge — captures uploaded, the team's own process map generated, a proposal written — or null while the automation is not being set up (and whenever it has no module process for the facts to hang off).

viewer_can_edit.description: Whether the caller may change this automation. An automation takes its agents' ownership rule: a Builder may edit one whose every agent they created, and Lead Builder or above may edit any. Sent by the list and detail endpoints; absent from create and update responses, where the client falls back to the caller's role.

post.description: Create a new automation. Its first agent is created alongside it so the caller lands on something editable; `first_agent` seeds that agent's name, configuration, and connections instead of the defaults. On a team on revision semantics the automation holds a single draft revision and no live revision, with the agent's first build bound into that draft, and the first activation makes the draft revision 1; on any other team the automation is a bare container and the build stands on its own.

get.description: Get case status counts for many Queues in ONE call. Use this after listQueues whenever you need per-Queue counts — cases waiting on a human, needing review, pending, failed — instead of calling listCases or searchCases once per Queue. Results are keyed by Queue ID and include zero counts for Queues with no matching cases; Queue IDs from other teams are silently dropped. For a count on a single Queue with richer filters, listCases with count_only=true is the alternative.

parameters.name: queue_ids

parameters.name: created_at_to
parameters.description: Exclusive case creation upper bound. Use an ISO 8601 timestamp or a relative duration such as 7d or 12h. Omit it for no upper bound.

waiting.description: Deprecated alias of needs_input. Read needs_input instead.

get.description: List runs for the current team. Supports filtering by agent, user, queue, status, etc. Messages, evaluation data, and queue metadata are included where available. Set count_only=true to skip Run row selection and enrichment. The normal response shape is returned with data: [] and the matching total. To sweep a whole team, follow `next_cursor` rather than raising `offset`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of runs per page (1-100, default 20)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of runs to skip. Every skipped run is still read by the database, so deep offsets get slower page by page; to walk a whole team's history, page with `cursor` instead.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Resume after the run a previous page ended on: pass the `next_cursor` that page returned, with the same filters and sort_order. Unlike offset, a cursor page does not re-read the runs before it, so a sweep does not slow down as it goes deeper; send `include_total=false` on the first page to skip the full count too. Runs created in between cannot shift a boundary already passed, so pages do not repeat or skip runs the way offset pages do. A run created or completed while a sweep is in progress can still be missed by that sweep, so to export runs continuously, poll with `since` and a short overlap and deduplicate on run id. Cannot be combined with `offset`. 400 when the value is not a valid runs cursor.

parameters.name: include_total
parameters.description: Whether to return `total`, the count of every matching run. Counting walks every match, so it costs far more than the page itself on a large team. Defaults to true on a first page and false on a `cursor` page, where `total` is null unless this is true. Implied by `count_only`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter to runs with this status

parameters.name: agent_id
parameters.description: Filter to runs for this agent

parameters.name: automation_id
parameters.description: Filter to runs that ran under this automation. A run keeps the automation it was created under, even after its agent moves to another automation

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Filter to runs owned by this user. Callers below Administrator, other than Lead Builders, are scoped to themselves regardless of this value, unless the request comes from a dashboard

parameters.name: case_queue_id
parameters.description: Filter to runs associated with this queue

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Filter to runs created from this source (e.g. api, schedule)

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Full-text search across run titles and case titles

parameters.name: has_issues
parameters.description: Filter on the run's latest successful evaluation: true returns only runs it flagged, false only runs it did not. Only the latest evaluation counts — an older flag does not match — and a run whose latest evaluation errored, or that has none, counts as unflagged. Omit to return both.

parameters.name: issue_severity
parameters.description: If set, only return runs whose latest successful evaluation has at least one failing rubric with this severity (critical | medium | low). Implies has_issues; legacy evaluations without severity companion fields do not match this filter.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return runs completed at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp. Runs that have not completed are excluded.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Return runs completed before this ISO-8601 timestamp. The upper bound is exclusive. Runs that have not completed are excluded.

parameters.name: count_only
parameters.description: Skip row selection and enrichment. The normal list response shape is returned with an empty row array and the matching total.

agent_type.description: Flavour of the step: "agent" for an agentic step, "code" for a deterministic code step. Fixed at creation — a step's builds all belong to the matching config family.

total.description: Total runs matching the filters, ignoring pagination. Null when no count was requested (a `cursor` page without `include_total=true`, or `include_total=false`) — distinct from a count of 0.

has_more.description: Whether another page exists past this one, determined by looking one row ahead. False on a count_only response.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` (same filters, same sort_order) to fetch the next page. Null when `has_more` is false. Continues right after the last run on this page.

get.description: Cross-process portfolio digest for every completed Clarity process on the team: per-process summary, SWOT, projected impact, and a step skeleton (role, system, and flow edges) — without step prose or source excerpts. Paginated (default 5, max 10). Use this to answer portfolio-wide questions in one pass; fetch a single process's full detail via getClarityProcessSnapshot only for the few that matter.

strengths.description: Internal advantages of the current process — capabilities, resources, or design choices that work in its favour today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Bartenders know regulars by name, which keeps service personal during peak hours."

weaknesses.description: Internal limitations of the current process — gaps, inefficiencies, or fragile assumptions visible in how it runs today. Phrase each as a short, evidence-backed statement. Example: "Manual pour times balloon during rushes because there is only one tap."

opportunities.description: External openings the current process could exploit — adjacent automations, scale effects, or unmet needs surfaced by the captures. Example: "POS data could feed dynamic pricing for slow hours."

threats.description: External risks that could degrade the current process — regulatory, operational, technological, or human factors visible in the captures. Example: "New ID-check legislation will require staff to interrupt every order."

Invite one person to a team. Pass `processId` to invite them to a specific Clarity process instead of the whole team (that requires the `team:clarity-member` role).
